papers.finding: Bystander CPR increased 30-day survival odds (aOR 1.70, 95% CI 1.24-2.34); good-quality CPR aOR 2.62 (95% CI 1.86-3.68); poor-quality CPR no benefit (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.68-1.45).
papers.caveat: Bystander CPR quality recorded in only 62.1% of cases and paramedic-assessed, so misclassification likely
papers.shortTitle: Good-quality bystander CPR triples OHCA survival

papers.title: Estimated survival gains from pulselessness-detection technologies in unwitnessed out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in Western Australia: a simulation study
papers.summary: WA simulation modelling across 11,450 OHCA cases estimated wearable pulselessness-detection could double 30-day survival among unwitnessed arrests (0.5% to 1.1%) with 10% device uptake and 80% sensitivity.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Australian regional research quantifying potential survival gains from a technology entering paramedic practice.
papers.design: Counterfactual simulation modelling using WA registry data
papers.n: 11,450 EMS-attended non-traumatic OHCA cases aged ≥16
papers.finding: With 100% device uptake and 100% sensitivity, 693 additional survivors over 5 years (survival 0.5% to 8.3%); with 10% uptake and 80% sensitivity, 52 additional survivors (survival 0.5% to 1.1%).
papers.caveat: Simulation based on modelled assumptions; no real-world device performance data
papers.shortTitle: Wearables could double unwitnessed OHCA survival

papers.title: Implementation of double sequential defibrillation (DSD): an Aotearoa New Zealand observational study
papers.summary: NZ EMS observational study (n=1,401) found no survival benefit after DSD implementation for refractory VF/VT, with lower ROSC odds in DSD patients likely reflecting confounding by indication.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Australasian context relevant to services using DSD, but findings may be confounded and timing guidance remains unclear.
papers.design: Retrospective pre/post observational cohort
papers.n: 1,401 patients with refractory VF/VT (pre 663, post 738)
papers.finding: No significant difference in ROSC or 30-day survival after DSD implementation; DSD patients had lower odds of ROSC (aOR 0.59, 95% CI 0.41-0.85) and late-DSD aOR 0.46 (95% CI 0.30-0.71).
papers.caveat: Confounding by indication — DSD used in patients with poorest prognosis
papers.shortTitle: Double sequential defibrillation shows no benefit

papers.title: Defining Diagnostic Excellence and Missed Diagnostic Opportunity for the Emergency Department Setting
papers.summary: Consensus study using a modified RAND/UCLA panel method to define diagnostic excellence and missed diagnostic opportunity in emergency departments — diagnostic excellence is accurate, timely, evidence-based, and patient-centered communication of a diagnosis based on available information, while a missed diagnostic opportunity is a measurable divergence from optimal practice that may lead to inaccurate/delayed explanations or communication failures.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Relevant concepts for paramedic diagnostic practice and handover communication, but ED-focused definitions rather than prehospital-specific
papers.design: Modified RAND/UCLA Delphi consensus panel
papers.n: 11 multidisciplinary expert panelists
papers.finding: Consensus definitions: diagnostic excellence is optimal, evidence-based practice to attain an accurate, timely, patient-centred, equitable explanation communicated to the patient; a missed diagnostic opportunity is a measurable divergence from optimal practice that may lead to inaccurate/delayed explanation or communication failure.
papers.caveat: Expert consensus definitions not yet validated or implemented
papers.shortTitle: Defining diagnostic excellence in the ED

papers.title: Intranasal Versus Subcutaneous Ketamine for the Treatment of Acute Traumatic Pain in the Emergency Department: A Randomized Clinical Trial
papers.summary: RCT testing whether intranasal ketamine is non-inferior to subcutaneous for acute traumatic pain — both routes provided equivalent analgesia with minimal clinically important differences, though minor adverse events were more common with subcutaneous administration.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Directly relevant to prehospital analgesia; IN route already used by many Australian services, confirms efficacy versus SC.
papers.design: Randomised double-blinded double-dummy trial
papers.n: 1,194 adults (599 subcutaneous, 595 intranasal) with acute musculoskeletal trauma
papers.finding: Mean NRS reduction at 30 min −4.42 (intranasal) vs −3.70 (subcutaneous), difference −0.72 (95% CI −0.95 to −0.48), below the 1.3 clinically important threshold; more minor adverse events with subcutaneous
papers.caveat: ED-based study of adults aged 18–65 using fixed 20 mg dose; prehospital relevance unclear
papers.shortTitle: Intranasal equals subcutaneous ketamine for pain

papers.title: Trauma undertriage at a University Hospital in North Norway: the need to look beyond mechanism of injury
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Retrospective registry study assessing trauma undertriage using ISS ≥16 and NISS ≥16 as reference — found 15% undertriage (above the recommended <5%), with 63% of undertriaged patients meeting national criteria but not receiving trauma team activation, mostly low-energy falls.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Relevant to Australian paramedics triaging trauma patients; low-energy falls are common presentations and this highlights risks of undertriage.
papers.design: Retrospective local trauma registry review
papers.n: 527 trauma patients (2018 and 2023)
papers.finding: Undertriage 15% by ISS≥16 and 18% by NISS≥16, exceeding recommended <5%; 63% of undertriaged patients met national trauma team activation criteria; 73% involved low-energy falls
papers.caveat: Single Scandinavian university hospital; retrospective design
papers.shortTitle: Trauma undertriage still high in Tromsø

papers.title: The use of Capnometry in Prehospital Intubation and Association with 30-Day Mortality: A Nationwide Registry Study
papers.summary: Nationwide registry study examining capnometry use during prehospital intubation and its association with 30-day mortality.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Directly relevant to Australian prehospital intubation practice; could inform guideline decisions on capnography/capnometry use.
papers.design: Nationwide retrospective registry cohort
papers.n: 8,625 patients (8,720 intubations) in Denmark 2016–2021
papers.finding: Capnometry used in 80.3% of intubations, rising from 75.4% to 82.6%; 30-day mortality 62.6%; capnometry use independently associated with lower mortality (more frequent in survivors, 87% vs 76%)
papers.caveat: Observational registry design — association may reflect confounding by indication or case mix
papers.shortTitle: Capnometry with prehospital intubation cuts mortality

papers.title: Medical Screening of Adult Psychiatric Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department
papers.summary: Scoping review mapping medical screening practices for adult psychiatric patients presenting to ED — identified 8 themes (laboratory testing, history taking, vital signs, physical examination, diagnostic imaging, screening tools, ECG, system-level factors), with society recommendations discouraging routine lab testing.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Prehospital clinicians frequently manage psychiatric presentations; findings on unnecessary testing patterns are relevant but ED-focused.
papers.design: Scoping review with thematic analysis
papers.n: 145 publications; 62 original studies covering 34,836 patients and 1,149 clinicians
papers.finding: Eight screening themes identified; laboratory testing most studied (62.9% of original studies); most society recommendations discourage routine laboratory testing
papers.caveat: Predominantly retrospective original studies; no assessment of diagnostic accuracy
papers.shortTitle: Mapping medical clearance of psychiatric ED patients

papers.title: Can physician-supervised medical students expand access to infant basic life support training? A prospective quasi-experimental study on long-term knowledge retention among caregivers
papers.summary: Quasi-experimental study testing whether physician-supervised medical students can deliver infant BLS training to caregivers — knowledge scores improved significantly after training and were sustained at 12 months, with no difference between physician and student-led groups.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Model for expanding community BLS training capacity; relevant to paramedic outreach programs though not clinical practice.
papers.design: Prospective quasi-experimental simulation-based training study
papers.n: 59 caregivers of infants (complete-case n=51)
papers.finding: Knowledge scores increased significantly after training (adjusted mean difference 8.0 points, 95% CI 7.1-8.9), sustained at 12 months with no difference between physician- and student-led groups (p=0.093); private-sector caregivers scored higher (1.3 points, 95% CI 0.5-2.1).
papers.caveat: Quasi-experimental, small sample, exploratory — supports feasibility under supervision, not equivalence
papers.shortTitle: Medical students can teach infant BLS

papers.title: Impact of pre-arrest glycemic state induced by prolonged fasting on defibrillation requirements: a prospective porcine model of ventricular fibrillation cardiac arrest
papers.summary: Porcine model of ventricular fibrillation cardiac arrest found that prolonged fasting-induced lower pre-arrest glycemia was associated with increased defibrillation requirements (median 2 vs 1 shock) and longer CPR duration, despite similar sustained ROSC rates.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Animal model provides mechanistic insight but can't be directly applied to human resuscitation practice. Glycemic state is not routinely assessed in cardiac arrest.
papers.design: Prospective randomised porcine model of VF cardiac arrest
papers.n: 20 male Landrace pigs randomised to 36-h or 12-h fasting
papers.finding: 36-h fasting group needed more shocks (median 2 vs 1, P=0.035) and longer CPR (median 344 s vs 191 s, P=0.043); sustained ROSC similar (70% vs 90%, P=0.582); higher pre-arrest glucose associated with fewer shocks (IRR 0.980 per mg/dL, P=0.002)
papers.caveat: Animal model, small sample, limited translation to human OHCA
papers.shortTitle: Prolonged fasting raises defibrillation needs in pigs

papers.title: Clinical outcomes and opportunities for improvement across modified trauma quality improvement cohorts: a registry-based cohort study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Registry-based cohort study of 8,298 trauma patients found that blunt multisystem cohorts had the highest opportunities-for-improvement rates (10.6% with TBI, 16.9% without) across multiple quality domains including potentially preventable deaths and clinical judgement errors.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Scandinavian registry data; patterns may differ in Australian systems. Descriptive study identifies problems but doesn't test interventions.
papers.design: Registry-based single-centre cohort with peer review
papers.n: 8,298 trauma patients at Karolinska University Hospital (2013-2023)
papers.finding: Blunt multisystem cohorts had highest opportunities-for-improvement rates (10.6% with TBI, 16.9% without), including potentially preventable deaths and clinical judgement errors; isolated severe TBI had highest mortality (52.8%) but no excess OFI
papers.caveat: Single university trauma centre, may not generalise to other systems
papers.shortTitle: Trauma quality improvement opportunities by cohort

papers.title: Fitting in or standing out: a scoping review of gender-related findings in Nordic EMS through an organizational socialization lens
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Scoping review of gender-related findings in Nordic EMS found women reported higher physical and psychosocial work demands, greater concerns about violence, and higher levels of mental health problems and sleep disturbances compared to male colleagues.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Nordic context with different workforce structures and regulations. Themes of workplace strain and violence are relevant but findings may not directly translate to Australian services.
papers.design: Scoping review (JBI/PRISMA-ScR)
papers.n: 7 peer-reviewed studies and 5 master's theses, 2010-2025
papers.finding: Women reported higher physical and psychosocial work demands (43% vs 22%; 41% vs 20%), greater concerns about threats and violence (58% vs 38%), and higher rates of mental health problems (29% vs 8%) and sleep disturbance (60% vs 39%)
papers.caveat: Only three studies explicitly examined gender; Nordic-specific findings with limited generalisability
papers.shortTitle: Gender gaps in Nordic EMS workplace

papers.title: Patterns of Online Medical Direction Utilization in an Urban EMS System: A Retrospective Analysis of 9,944 Consultations
papers.summary: Retrospective analysis of 9,944 online medical direction consultations from 2016-2024 found OLMD is primarily used for patient refusals (65%) with 97% physician approval, and overall ~93% agreement between paramedic requests and physician decisions
papers.relevance: 🟢 High transferability — Large real-world EMS dataset directly applicable to OLMD practice patterns and protocol refinement
papers.design: Retrospective descriptive analysis of consultation records
papers.n: 9,944 online medical direction consultations (2016-2024)
papers.finding: Patient refusals accounted for 65% (n=5,175) of consultations with 97% physician approval; termination of resuscitation and transport destination requests approved in 98% and 90%; overall physician agreement ~93%
papers.caveat: Single urban US (border) EMS system, may not generalise to Australian practice
papers.shortTitle: Online medical direction mostly for refusals

papers.title: Incidence and impact of loss of pulsatility on outcomes after extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation – A retrospective cohort study
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort of 221 ECPR patients found loss of pulsatility (zero pulse pressure) occurred in 49% of cases and was associated with significantly higher in-hospital mortality (74% vs 48%), with each additional hour of non-pulsatility increasing mortality risk by 17%
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium transferability — Highly specialized ECMO center study with limited direct prehospital relevance, though useful for understanding ECPR prognostication
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre cohort
papers.n: 221 ECPR patients
papers.finding: Loss of pulsatility occurred in 49% (108/221); in-hospital mortality 74% vs 48% (p=0.01); each additional hour of non-pulsatility increased mortality risk (OR 1.17, 95% CI 1.05–1.30)
papers.caveat: Retrospective, single high-volume ECMO centre; loss of pulsatility group had more OHCA and longer arrest-to-ECMO times
papers.shortTitle: Loss of pulsatility predicts death after ECPR

papers.title: Non-urgent emergency department utilization in adults: a systematic review of associated factors across diverse health systems
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Systematic review of 32 studies across 21 countries identified factors associated with non-urgent ED utilisation, with frequent prior ED visits (aOR up to 82) and patient perception of non-serious illness (aOR up to 21) being the strongest predictors
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium transferability — Provides operational context for understanding ED utilisation patterns, though in-hospital focus
papers.design: Systematic review of cross-sectional, cohort and case-control studies
papers.n: 32 studies, 21 countries
papers.finding: Non-urgent visit proportion 1–82.4%; strongest associations with frequent prior ED visits (aOR up to 82.13) and patient perception of non-serious illness (aOR up to 21.03)
papers.caveat: Substantial heterogeneity in definitions of non-urgent visits; narrative synthesis only
papers.shortTitle: Who makes non-urgent ED visits

papers.title: Effect of an app-guided advanced cardiac life support algorithm on teamwork, non-technical skills, and workload in simulated in-hospital cardiac arrest: a randomized controlled feasibility trial
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Randomized simulation trial of 40 teams testing the 'CPR Leader' app during in-hospital cardiac arrest found no meaningful improvement in team performance, non-technical skills, or ALS algorithm adherence compared to control
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium transferability — Simulation-based in-hospital study shows mobile decision support tools may not deliver expected benefits, but limited prehospital transferability
papers.design: Randomised simulation-based feasibility trial
papers.n: 40 two-person teams (80 participants)
papers.finding: No meaningful between-group differences in TEAM, ANTS or NASA-TLX scores (workload 49.2 vs 54.1, p=0.2); ALS metrics similar except earlier compressions in control group in VF
papers.caveat: Simulation feasibility trial with predominantly experienced in-hospital clinicians; authors note findings should not be generalised to novices or prehospital settings
papers.shortTitle: CPR leader app no help in simulation

papers.title: Distribution of visual attention amongst clinicians using an augmented reality-based decision support system during simulated cardiac arrest – A descriptive study
papers.summary: Secondary analysis of a pediatric cardiac arrest simulation trial found AR-based decision support captured 42-59% of visual attention with distinct role-specific fixation patterns among team leaders and medication nurses
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium transferability — Small simulation study (9 sessions) provides insight into how AR cognitive aids might affect attention, though pediatric in-hospital setting limits direct relevance
papers.design: Descriptive secondary analysis of simulation RCT intervention arm with eye tracking
papers.n: 9 paediatric resuscitation simulation sessions
papers.finding: AR components captured 41.9% (team leaders) and 59.0% (medication nurses) of visual attention; attention outside predefined areas was 46.0% and 22.9% respectively
papers.caveat: Descriptive analysis of only nine simulation sessions; no outcome data
papers.shortTitle: AR decision support grabs clinician gaze

papers.title: Prehospital national early warning score outperforms shock index in predicting mortality and resource utilisation in adult trauma: A systematic review
papers.summary: Systematic review of 22 studies (184 to 1.4M patients) found prehospital NEWS showed excellent discrimination for short-term mortality (AUROC 0.87-0.96) and reliably predicted transfusion needs, outperforming Shock Index.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Directly relevant to prehospital trauma triage, large evidence base across diverse EMS systems with clear clinical application.
papers.design: Systematic review of prognostic accuracy studies
papers.n: 22 studies, 184 to 1,439,221 adult trauma patients
papers.finding: Prehospital NEWS showed excellent discrimination for short-term mortality (AUROC 0.87-0.96) and predicted transfusion and resource use; shock index performed worse (AUROC 0.48-0.79), with NEWS outperforming SI across all mortality endpoints
papers.caveat: Substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations and outcome measures meant only narrative synthesis was possible
papers.shortTitle: Prehospital NEWS beats shock index in trauma

papers.title: Prehospital Whole Blood Administration in Adults With Hemorrhagic Shock and Its Association With Shock Physiology and Clinical Outcomes: A Systematic Review
papers.summary: Systematic review of 13 studies found prehospital whole blood consistently improved shock physiology (greater SI reduction, higher shock reversal rates) and showed potential survival benefit in high-risk and penetrating trauma patients, though overall mortality benefit was not uniform.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Directly relevant to prehospital blood product protocols, growing evidence base with clear physiologic advantages over component therapy.
papers.design: Systematic review
papers.n: 13 studies of adults with haemorrhagic shock
papers.finding: Mortality differences were not significant (24-h: 15.8% vs 11.2%; 28-day: 25.0% vs 26.1%, P=0.85), but whole blood was consistently associated with greater shock index reduction (0.43 vs 0.10, P<0.05) and potential survival benefit in select high-risk populations
papers.caveat: Variable mortality findings across heterogeneous studies; no uniform survival benefit demonstrated
papers.shortTitle: Prehospital whole blood improves shock physiology

papers.title: Independent predictors of hyperoxemia following prehospital oxygen therapy: A prospective cohort study
papers.journal: The American Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Prospective cohort of 245 patients found 24.5% had hyperoxemia (PaO₂ >120 mmHg), with intubation (OR 38.89) and transport duration ≥24 min (OR 13.74) as independent predictors.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Directly relevant to daily paramedic practice, clear actionable findings about oxygen titration and reassessment during transport.
papers.design: Prospective single-centre cohort
papers.n: 245 adults transported by ambulance receiving oxygen
papers.finding: 24.5% were hyperoxaemic (PaO2 >120 mmHg) on ED arrival; independent predictors were intubation (OR 38.89) and transport duration ≥24 min (OR 13.74); ED SpO2 ≥96.5% predicted hyperoxaemia with AUC 0.70
papers.caveat: Single-centre study at one tertiary ED, limiting generalisability
papers.shortTitle: Predictors of hyperoxaemia after prehospital oxygen

papers.title: Establishment of an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest registry in Penang, Malaysia
papers.summary: Descriptive analysis of 5,087 OHCA cases showed 16.3% received EMS resuscitation attempts, with only 1.3% 30-day survival despite bystander CPR in 43.5% of cases, and AED deployment in only 7.1%.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Valuable registry data but from Malaysia with different EMS system and longer response times (median 21 min), though low AED deployment findings are broadly relevant.
papers.design: Descriptive analysis of first-year registry data (Utstein template)
papers.n: 5,087 OHCA cases
papers.finding: 16.3% had an EMS resuscitation attempt; bystander CPR in 43.5%, AED applied in 7.1%, ROSC in 10.3%, 30-day survival 1.3%; median ambulance response time 21 min
papers.caveat: Descriptive single-region data from a newly established registry with very different EMS system to Australia
papers.shortTitle: New Penang OHCA registry shows low survival

papers.title: Ambient oxygen enrichment during cardiopulmonary resuscitation: an overestimated risk? - Insights from a manikin study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Mannequin study testing whether removing oxygen-delivery devices reduces ambient oxygen concentration at defibrillation sites — it found no clinically relevant oxygen accumulation, and removing devices made no difference to oxygen levels.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Directly challenges current ERC guideline (followed by Australian services) requiring oxygen device removal before defibrillation; could simplify CPR workflow if adopted.
papers.design: Controlled mannequin-based simulation study
papers.n: 20 resuscitation scenarios; 6,555 oxygen measurements
papers.finding: Median ambient oxygen 21.6% (IQR 21.3–22.1%); removing oxygen delivery devices >1 m did not lower oxygen concentrations; intubation and OxyDemand valve gave slightly lower fractions
papers.caveat: Mannequin simulation with limited scenarios; may not reflect real arrests with leaks or high-flow oxygen
papers.shortTitle: No risky oxygen build-up at defibrillation site in CPR

papers.title: Location-resolved performance of public-access defibrillation in an urban EMS system: a population-based study in Yokohama, Japan
papers.summary: Population-based study of public-access defibrillation performance across different locations in urban Yokohama, Japan
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Relevant to PAD deployment strategies but abstract not available for detailed assessment
papers.design: Retrospective population-based registry study with propensity score matching
papers.n: 15,345 OHCA patients in Yokohama, Japan, 2021–2024 (272 received PAD shock)
papers.finding: PAD shock associated with favourable 30-day neurological outcome (OR 3.3; 95% CI 1.9–5.7) and 30-day survival (OR 3.7; 95% CI 2.2–6.1); shock rates varied by location from 34% at sports facilities to 0.06% at private residences
papers.caveat: Japanese urban setting; very few PAD shocks overall, and residual confounding possible despite matching
papers.shortTitle: Public-access defibrillation location effects in Yokohama

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Golden Hour: A scoping review of prehospital trauma triage and implementation feasibility in LMICs
papers.summary: Scoping review mapping AI applications in LMIC prehospital trauma care found ML models achieved AUC 0.91-0.94 for mortality prediction and digital platforms reduced response times from 162 to 13 minutes in Bangladesh.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — AI/ML methods are methodologically relevant, but study focused on LMIC contexts (Indonesia, Kenya, Bangladesh, Tanzania) with very different infrastructure and system constraints than Australia.
papers.design: Scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) of AI in LMIC prehospital trauma care
papers.n: 17 primary studies
papers.finding: ML models achieved AUC 0.91–0.94 for mortality prediction; digital platforms in Bangladesh reduced average response times from 162 to 13 minutes; edge-AI/NLP achieved 95% accuracy in low-connectivity settings
papers.caveat: Scoping review of heterogeneous LMIC studies; no appraisal of patient outcomes
papers.shortTitle: AI trauma triage in LMIC prehospital care

papers.title: Paramedic perspectives on prehospital buprenorphine: A qualitative case study of implementation in emergency medical services
papers.journal: The American Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Abstract not yet available (ahead-of-print). Qualitative case study of paramedic perspectives on prehospital buprenorphine implementation in emergency medical services.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Relevant clinical topic (OUD treatment with buprenorphine) but no abstract yet and likely US-focused based on journal.
papers.design: Qualitative embedded case study with semi-structured interviews
papers.n: 6 paramedics
papers.finding: Five themes: scene context and competing priorities, perceived value of buprenorphine, clinician comfort/exposure, importance of follow-up, and logistical/operational barriers; uptake driven by system-level rather than clinical factors
papers.caveat: Very small sample from a single early-stage program; limited transferability
papers.shortTitle: Paramedic views on prehospital buprenorphine

papers.title: Incidence, aetiologies and survival outcomes of paediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in Singapore
papers.summary: Abstract not yet available (ahead-of-print). Observational study reporting incidence, aetiologies and survival outcomes of paediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in Singapore.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Paediatric OHCA is directly relevant to Australian paramedic practice; Singapore provides a useful regional comparator with similar urban EMS systems.
papers.design: Retrospective analysis of a prospective registry (PAROS) with descriptive and multivariate analysis
papers.n: 414 patients aged <18 years with OHCA in Singapore, 2010–2021
papers.finding: Incidence 4.62 per 100,000 person-years (infants 33.5); bystander CPR 64.5%; aetiologies respiratory 21%, drowning 20.2%, trauma 18.5%; ROSC 35.5%, 30-day survival 11.1%, good neurological outcome 8%; 30-day survival improved in 2019–2021 vs 2010–2012 (aOR 4.34; 95% CI 1.09–17.22)
papers.caveat: Single-country registry data; wide confidence interval on the survival trend
papers.shortTitle: Singapore paediatric OHCA incidence and survival

papers.title: Bag size for manual ventilation during cardiopulmonary resuscitation in adult cardiac arrest: a systematic review
papers.summary: Systematic review testing whether smaller self-inflating bags improve CPR outcomes — they found limited very-low-certainty evidence suggesting smaller bags (450-700mL) were associated with lower survival with favourable neuro outcomes compared to standard adult bags (1000-1685mL).
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Directly relevant to prehospital CPR practice — bag valve choice is a standard clinical decision and these findings challenge the assumption that smaller bags are safer for airway protection during CPR.
papers.design: Systematic review (ILCOR Continuous Evidence Evaluation, GRADE)
papers.n: One observational study of 1994 OHCA patients plus two simulation cross-over studies
papers.finding: Smaller bags (450–700 mL) were associated with lower survival with favourable neurological outcome (AOR 0.65, 95% CI 0.43–0.99) and lower event survival (AOR 0.73, 95% CI 0.60–0.90) versus standard adult bags (1000–1685 mL); no randomised trials identified
papers.caveat: Very-low certainty evidence from a single before-and-after observational study and no randomised trials
papers.shortTitle: Smaller bags worse for CPR ventilation

papers.title: Emergency medical service organizational structure and prehospital outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in China: Insights from the BASIC-OHCA
papers.summary: Retrospective analysis of 24,814 OHCA patients comparing independent EMS models with hospital-based models in China — the independent model had higher survived event rates (2.23% vs 1.40%) despite longer response times.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Organizational structure is relevant to Australian services, but China's EMS context differs significantly — still offers useful comparative data on system design and its impact on OHCA outcomes.
papers.design: Retrospective registry cohort comparing EMS organisational models
papers.n: 24,814 OHCA patients across 10 EMS systems in China
papers.finding: Survived event rate (ROSC sustained to ED handover) was 2.05% overall; independent EMS model 2.23% vs hospital-based 1.40% (P<0.05), despite longer response times in the independent model
papers.caveat: Retrospective Chinese data with very small absolute difference (0.83%); not generalisable to Australian EMS systems
papers.shortTitle: Independent EMS beats hospital-based model in Chinese OHCA

papers.title: Impact of calcium administration on survival and neurologic outcomes in adults with in-hospital cardiac arrest
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort study of 599 in-hospital cardiac arrest patients testing whether calcium administration improves outcomes — calcium was associated with significantly lower rates of sustained ROSC, survival to discharge, and favourable neuro outcomes.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — In-hospital context limits direct prehospital applicability, but findings support current guideline recommendations against routine calcium use during undifferentiated cardiac arrest.
papers.design: Retrospective cohort from a prospective single-centre registry
papers.n: 599 adult in-hospital cardiac arrest events (234 received calcium)
papers.finding: Calcium associated with lower sustained ROSC (31.6% vs 57.8%), survival to discharge (6.8% vs 18.9%) and favourable neurological outcome (3.0% vs 14.3%), independently on multivariable analysis
papers.caveat: Single US tertiary centre, retrospective; confounding by indication likely despite adjustment
papers.shortTitle: Calcium in in-hospital arrest linked to worse outcomes

papers.title: Where should we compress? Ultrasound identification of the ideal area of maximal compression for CPR
papers.summary: Prospective observational study using transthoracic echocardiography to map optimal chest compression location — guideline-recommended hand placement frequently overlies the left ventricular outflow tract rather than the ideal area of maximal compression.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Anatomically relevant to CPR technique, but requires ultrasound for application — the finding that standard compression points may not be optimal is worth noting, though practice change would need stronger outcome evidence.
papers.design: Prospective observational echocardiographic mapping study
papers.n: 152 adult ED patients and volunteers
papers.finding: Guideline hand position overlies the LVOT (median 1.5 cm from sternum) rather than the ideal area of maximal compression (median 4 cm lateral); LVOT within 1 cm of sternum in 50% vs 2.7% for iAMC
papers.caveat: Anatomical mapping in non-arrest subjects; no link shown to CPR outcomes
papers.shortTitle: Ultrasound maps CPR hand position over LVOT not iAMC

papers.title: Willingness to act in a cardiac arrest and awareness of automated external defibrillators: a survey of the Swedish population
papers.summary: Population-based survey found 80% of Swedish adults willing to perform CPR on a stranger, with recent training increasing confidence and awareness, but only 20% know where their nearest AED is located at home.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Relevant to understanding bystander CPR willingness and AED awareness barriers, but Swedish-specific data may not directly translate to Australian community context.
papers.design: Population-based cross-sectional survey of a Swedish online panel
papers.n: 1026 adults aged 18–84 years
papers.finding: 80% would act if a stranger had a cardiac arrest; ~half felt confident using an AED; 50% knew the nearest AED at work but only ~20% at home; recent CPR training was associated with greater willingness to act
papers.caveat: Survey of a single country's population; self-reported willingness may not reflect actual behaviour
papers.shortTitle: Swedish public CPR willingness and AED awareness

papers.title: Neuroprotection via optimizing cerebral blood flow after cardiac arrest (neuro-intact) study – A phase II proof-of-concept study protocol
papers.summary: Phase II protocol testing whether individualised MAP targets derived from real-time cerebral autoregulation monitoring reduce secondary brain injury after cardiac arrest — this proof-of-concept trial uses near-infrared spectroscopy and transcranial Doppler to identify each patient's optimal MAP rather than applying uniform targets.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Protocol study without results yet — the concept of individualised post-arrest blood pressure targets is promising and relevant to Australian practice, but clinical utility depends on trial outcomes showing actual benefit.
papers.design: Phase II single-arm proof-of-concept trial protocol using NIRS and transcranial Doppler to derive individualised optimal MAP
papers.n: 49 comatose OHCA survivors within 12 h of ROSC
papers.caveat: Protocol only, no results; single-centre, single-arm, surrogate endpoints
papers.shortTitle: Individualised MAP targets after OHCA (protocol)

papers.title: National Patterns of Pediatric Emergency Department Utilization by Arrival Mode and Geographic Setting: Final Data from the National Hospital Ambulatory Medical Care Survey 2016–2022
papers.summary: Retrospective analysis of 202.5 million US pediatric ED visits (2016–2022) found children comprised only 7% of EMS transports but presented with higher acuity, more abnormal vital signs, and increasing psychiatric and behavioral presentations over time.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Descriptive US epidemiology — the trend toward increasing pediatric psych/behavioral EMS encounters likely reflects similar patterns in Australia and informs system planning, though absolute numbers and specifics will differ between health systems.
papers.design: Cross-sectional analysis of nationally representative US survey (NHAMCS) with survey weights
papers.n: 202.5 million estimated paediatric ED visits 2016–2022, including 9.0 million EMS arrivals
papers.finding: Children were ~7% of EMS transports; EMS-arriving children had higher acuity triage (29.8% vs 8.5%), admission/transfer (24.9% vs 5.3%) and ≥1 abnormal vital sign (40.4% vs 22.6%); psychiatric/behavioural/substance-use conditions were ~12% of paediatric EMS encounters and increased over time
papers.caveat: US data and survey estimates, so may not generalise to Australian systems
papers.shortTitle: US paediatric ED use: low EMS share, high acuity

papers.title: Cold-water immersion during out-of-hospital heatstroke cardiac arrest resuscitation: feasible but futile?
papers.summary: Examines feasibility and outcomes of cold-water immersion during prehospital heatstroke cardiac arrest resuscitation
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low — No abstract available — cannot assess findings or applicability to Australian practice
papers.shortTitle: Cold-water immersion in heatstroke cardiac arrest

papers.title: The Prevalence of Adverse Events After Prehospital Neuromuscular Blockade-Assisted Airway Management
papers.summary: Investigates the prevalence of adverse events following prehospital airway management using neuromuscular blockade
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low — No abstract available — cannot assess safety outcomes or transferability without full text
papers.design: Cross-sectional analysis of 2023 NEMSIS national dataset
papers.n: 11,525 adult prehospital neuromuscular blockade-assisted airway cases
papers.finding: 27.5% had at least one adverse event within 10 minutes: hypoxemia 25.0%, hypotension 15.0%, bradycardia 2.7%, cardiac arrest 1.9%; first pass success 80.6%; abnormal pre-blockade vitals markedly increased odds (e.g. hypotension OR 16.8, 95% CI 13.1-21.8)
papers.caveat: Administrative dataset with no chart-level verification; excludes cardiac arrest cases; US data only
papers.shortTitle: High adverse event rate after prehospital RSI

papers.title: The estimated prevalence of multiple record encounters in the National Emergency Medical Services Information System
papers.summary: Retrospective analysis of 36.7 million NEMSIS records — 99.5% represent unique patient-care episodes with only 0.5% involving multiple records for the same encounter
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium transferability — Australian paramedics don't use NEMSIS, but data quality issues are universal for anyone doing EMS research or evaluating large datasets
papers.design: Retrospective observational analysis of NEMSIS 2023 dataset using record-clustering algorithm
papers.n: 36,757,562 EMS records
papers.finding: 99.5% of episodes of care consisted of a single EMS record; only ~0.5% involved multiple records for the same encounter
papers.caveat: Algorithm-based identification of related records; potential misclassification of clustered encounters
papers.shortTitle: NEMSIS records mostly unique encounters

papers.title: Family, Domestic and Sexual Violence Presentations to a Virtual Emergency Department: A Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort of Victoria's Virtual ED — only 21 FDSV presentations identified among 173,936 visits (0.012%), suggesting significant under-detection
papers.relevance: 🟢 High transferability — Direct Australian context, virtual EDs are expanding, and paramedics need awareness that FDSV presentations may be missed in telehealth settings
papers.design: Retrospective cohort study of Victorian Virtual Emergency Department presentations
papers.n: 173,936 VVED presentations, 21 FDSV cases identified
papers.finding: FDSV presentations were 0.012% of all visits; all female, median age 37 years; intimate partner violence most common (81%); head/face/neck injuries most frequent (53%); 76% referred by healthcare professionals
papers.caveat: Cases identified retrospectively via documentation, so figures likely reflect under-detection rather than true prevalence
papers.shortTitle: FDSV rarely detected in virtual ED

papers.title: The Safety of Single Aminoglycoside Dose in Emergency Departments (SAD-ED) Among Patients With and Without Chronic Kidney Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort across four Australian hospitals — single-dose aminoglycosides caused AKI in 30.9% of CKD patients vs 13.4% without CKD (OR 2.88)
papers.relevance: 🟢 High transferability — Australian study with direct clinical relevance — gentamicin is commonly given in ED/prehospital settings and CKD patients are at substantially higher risk
papers.design: Retrospective cohort at four Australian tertiary hospitals
papers.n: 660 ED patients who received single-dose aminoglycosides
papers.finding: AKI within 1 week occurred in 30.9% of CKD patients vs 13.4% without CKD (OR 2.88, 95% CI 1.76–4.71); CKD patients had more severe AKI (stage 2: 10.1% vs 2.6%)
papers.caveat: Retrospective design with confounding by indication — CKD patients were older with more comorbidities
papers.shortTitle: Single-dose aminoglycoside AKI risk in CKD

papers.title: The Sydney Triage to Admission Risk Tool With Artificial Intelligence (START-AI) to Support Decision Making in Emergency Departments: Model Explainability and Feature Importance Analysis
papers.summary: Model explainability analysis of START-AI — AUROC improved from 0.78 to 0.90 with AI features, driven primarily by blood test results, triage comments, and clinical notes
papers.relevance: 🟢 High transferability — Australian-developed tool with strong validation results; AI triage support is coming to pre-hospital care and this shows what features matter most
papers.design: Model explainability analysis of single-centre ED electronic medical record data over 2 years
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: AUROC for predicting inpatient admission improved from 0.78 (START alone) to 0.90 with all START-AI features; blood test results (lactate, CRP), triage comments and ED case notes contributed most, vital signs contributed little
papers.caveat: Single-centre data; prediction of admission rather than patient-centred outcomes
papers.shortTitle: AI triage tool predicts ED admission

papers.title: Vaccine Preventable Diseases in the Emergency Department
papers.summary: Editorial on the re-emergence of vaccine-preventable diseases post-COVID — declining vaccination rates are causing outbreaks of diphtheria, measles, and other VPDs in Australasia
papers.relevance: 🟢 High transferability — Directly relevant to paramedic occupational health and patient care — VPDs are presenting more frequently and require heightened awareness
papers.design: Editorial
papers.n: Not reported
papers.shortTitle: Vaccine-preventable diseases re-emerging in EDs

papers.title: Does the Emergency Department Have a Role in Immunisation? Yes—But Not as a Routine Vaccine Clinic
papers.summary: Editorial arguing EDs should provide opportunistic, proportionate immunisation for vulnerable patients rather than functioning as routine vaccine clinics
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium transferability — Relevant to understanding the role EDs (and by extension, paramedics) play in immunisation, though less directly actionable for pre-hospital care
papers.design: Editorial
papers.n: Not reported
papers.shortTitle: EDs: opportunistic immunisation, not vaccine clinics

papers.title: Refractory ventricular fibrillation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: shock characteristics, predictors and clinical outcomes
papers.summary: This registry study of 436 OHCA patients compared refractory VF (all three shocks failed to terminate, 5% of cases) versus recurrent VF, finding refractory VF patients had lower ROSC (41% vs 59%) and 30-day survival (23% vs 46%) with predictors including no CPR/AED before EMS, longer delay to first shock, and lower amplitude spectral area.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Directly relevant to OHCA VF management and defibrillation decision-making, though low event numbers limit certainty
papers.design: Registry cohort with ECG waveform analysis (ARREST registry)
papers.n: 436 patients with VF at first three rhythm checks; 22 with refractory VF
papers.finding: Refractory VF in 5% of cases; ROSC 41% vs 59% (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.41-1.15) and 30-day survival 23% vs 46% (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.23-1.08) versus recurrent VF; predictors included no bystander CPR/AED, longer delay to first shock, lower amplitude spectral area
papers.caveat: Only 22 refractory VF patients, so outcomes were underpowered and remain uncertain
papers.shortTitle: Refractory VF rare with worse outcomes

papers.title: Association of rescue breathing with outcomes in adult suffocation-related cardiac arrest
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort of 76,774 Japanese patients with witnessed suffocation-related OHCA found no bystander CPR was associated with higher favourable neurological outcomes compared with compression-only CPR (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.04-1.38), while CCV-CPR showed no significant difference versus compression-only.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Japanese-specific context and counterintuitive findings that require local validation before changing practice guidance
papers.design: Retrospective nationwide registry cohort with IPTW adjustment
papers.n: 76,774 adults with witnessed suffocation-related OHCA
papers.finding: No bystander CPR associated with better 1-month favourable neurological outcome than compression-only CPR (adjusted OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.04-1.38); CCV-CPR no significant difference (OR 1.01, 95% CI 0.78-1.32)
papers.caveat: Retrospective registry data with possible residual confounding; Japanese setting with different bystander CPR practices
papers.shortTitle: Bystander rescue breathing no benefit in suffocation OHCA

papers.title: Volume-controlled mechanical ventilation during cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.summary: This systematic review of 13 articles (six RCTs, seven non-randomised studies) found very low to low certainty evidence showing no significant difference in ROSC between volume-controlled mechanical ventilation and manual ventilation during CPR.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — Relevant to advanced airway management during cardiac arrest, but very low certainty evidence means no practice change warranted
papers.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science)
papers.n: 13 articles: six RCTs (461 patients) and seven non-randomised studies (4,607 patients)
papers.finding: Meta-analysis of 120 patients from two RCTs showed no difference in ROSC for volume-controlled versus manual ventilation (OR 1.31, 95% CI 0.64-2.71); certainty of evidence very low to low
papers.caveat: Very low to low certainty evidence; trials at low to high risk of bias, non-randomised studies at serious or critical risk
papers.shortTitle: Mechanical vs manual ventilation in CPR equal

papers.title: Perceived cognitive load among emergency department code blue teams: distribution, correlates and relationship with team performance
papers.summary: This multicentre cross-sectional study of 58 resuscitations found perceived cognitive load was highest among team leaders (mean 5.5/9) and higher team leader cognitive load was associated with higher load among team members and lower TEAM-assessed performance.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — Directly applicable to resuscitation team training and leadership, with clear implications for supporting team leaders during high-acuity events
papers.design: Multicentre cross-sectional study with prospective data collection in ED resuscitations
papers.n: 58 resuscitations, 228 healthcare professional observations
papers.finding: Team leaders had highest perceived cognitive load (mean 5.5, SD 1.7; β = 1.12, 95% CI 0.27-1.98); higher team leader load associated with higher team member load (β = 0.53) and lower TEAM-assessed performance
papers.caveat: Cross-sectional design using self-reported cognitive load; ED setting only, small sample
papers.shortTitle: Team leaders carry highest cognitive load

papers.title: Prehospital neuroprotectant in combination with post-arrival thrombolytic therapy for acute ischemic stroke. Secondary analysis of the FAST-MAG prehospital trial
papers.journal: Journal of Stroke and Cerebrovascular Diseases
papers.summary: Secondary analysis testing whether prehospital magnesium sulfate followed by thrombolysis improves 90-day outcomes — feasible and safe but no significant overall clinical benefit, though severe stroke patients (NIHSS >15) showed better outcomes in hypothesis-generating subgroup analysis.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Secondary analysis of the FAST-MAG phase 3 RCT
papers.n: 401 patients receiving thrombolysis (214 magnesium, 187 placebo)
papers.finding: No significant overall 90-day mRS benefit from prehospital magnesium plus thrombolysis; in severe strokes (NIHSS >15) the magnesium group had higher rates of favourable 90-day outcome (mRS 0-2); median last-known-well to prehospital infusion was 46 min and 93 min pre-thrombolysis exposure
papers.caveat: Secondary/subgroup analysis of a null trial; subgroup findings hypothesis-generating
papers.shortTitle: Prehospital magnesium before thrombolysis: no overall benefit

papers.title: National Characteristics of Emergency Medical Services in Rural and Frontier Areas: A 2024 Update on Rural-Urban Differences in EMS Care
papers.summary: Survey examining EMS characteristics and care differences between rural and urban areas — reports on resource availability, response times, and clinical capabilities.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Cross-sectional analysis of a national EMS registry (NEMSIS 2024)
papers.n: 45,383,694 EMS responses across 50 US states and DC; 6.9% rural
papers.finding: Rural responses showed older patients, greater air-medical use and higher on-scene mortality; the rural trauma on-scene death excess was largely explained by patient physiology at first EMS contact; the 2012 rural stroke-mortality gap was absent in 2024
papers.caveat: US registry data; limited to recorded NEMSIS variables
papers.shortTitle: Rural vs urban EMS: 2024 NEMSIS update

papers.title: Prehospital resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) in patients with major trauma and cardiac arrest: a systematic review
papers.summary: Systematic review evaluating prehospital REBOA for traumatic cardiac arrest — reports on feasibility, survival outcomes, and complications.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.design: Systematic review with narrative synthesis
papers.n: 18 included studies (case studies, cohorts, one trial); 38 civilian trauma, 90 civilian non-traumatic cardiac arrest and 2 combat REBOA cases
papers.finding: Successful prehospital REBOA deployment in 76% of civilian trauma and 84% of civilian non-traumatic cardiac arrest cases; survival to discharge 44% (14/32) in trauma, 4% (1/25) in OHCA, 88% (7/8) in interfacility transport; OHCA cases showed significant blood pressure/EtCO2 rises
papers.caveat: Critical-to-serious risk of bias; small numbers, almost no control groups
papers.shortTitle: Prehospital REBOA: feasibility shown, survival mixed

papers.title: Determinants of Timely Prehospital Thrombolysis Administration within a Pharmacoinvasive STEMI Network in Victoria, Australia
papers.summary: This Australian study identifies factors affecting timely prehospital thrombolysis delivery in Victoria's pharmacoinvasive STEMI network.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective registry cohort, Victorian Ambulance STEMI Quality Initiative
papers.n: 1440 adults treated with paramedic thrombolysis for suspected STEMI, 2018-2023
papers.finding: 32.5% received prehospital thrombolysis within 30 min of first medical contact (median 37 min); delay associated with mild pain severity (aOR 2.08), clinical consultation and after-hours presentation, while ECG within 10 min reduced delay (aOR 0.40); times improved 17% per year (aOR 0.83)
papers.caveat: Retrospective registry data; suspected rather than confirmed STEMI
papers.shortTitle: Only a third get PHT within 30 min

papers.title: Emergency Medical Services Physician-Led Activation for Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
papers.summary: Observational cohort testing an EMS physician-led prehospital ECPR activation protocol for refractory VT/VF cardiac arrest — only 4.3% of 347 OHCA patients were eligible, ECPR was activated in 66.7% of eligible patients, and 40% of the activation group survived to discharge with good neurological outcome.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Observational cohort of an EMS physician-led ECPR activation protocol
papers.n: 347 adults with non-traumatic OHCA, North Carolina, one year
papers.finding: Only 15/347 (4.3%) were ECPR-eligible; activated in 10/15 (66.7%); cannulation in 5/10; 40% (4/10) of activation group survived to discharge, all CPC 1; 3/5 non-activated eligible patients survived
papers.caveat: Single EMS agency, one year, very small numbers
papers.shortTitle: Physician-led prehospital ECPR: small eligible subset

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of prehospital whole blood resuscitation in traumatic haemorrhagic shock a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.journal: The American Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating outcomes of prehospital whole blood transfusion compared to blood component therapy in traumatic haemorrhagic shock.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
papers.n: 3 RCTs, 2048 adults with traumatic haemorrhagic shock
papers.finding: No significant difference between prehospital whole blood and blood components in 24-h mortality (OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.81-1.55), 28-30-day mortality (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.90-1.47), massive transfusion or thromboembolism; I2 = 0%
papers.caveat: Only three trials of limited size and quality
papers.shortTitle: No mortality benefit for prehospital whole blood

papers.title: Effect of bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation type on 1-month survival in drowning following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in natural water bodies: a nationwide retrospective cohort study
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort of 3914 drowning-related OHCA patients found conventional CPR (compressions with rescue breaths) was associated with higher 1-month survival compared with hands-only CPR (24.1% vs 9.4%), and both were superior to no CPR (2.7%).
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective nationwide registry cohort (Utstein, Japan 2016-2022)
papers.n: 3914 drowning-related OHCAs in natural water bodies
papers.finding: 1-month survival: no bystander CPR 2.7%, hands-only CPR 9.4%, conventional CPR 24.1%. Versus no CPR, conventional CPR AOR 3.70 (95% CI 2.31-5.93), hands-only AOR 1.74 (1.19-2.54); conventional CPR superior to hands-only (AOR 2.13, 95% CI 1.41-3.23).
papers.caveat: Retrospective registry data with residual confounding and only 232 patients (5.9%) receiving conventional CPR.
papers.shortTitle: Conventional CPR best for drowning OHCA

papers.title: Telemedicine-assisted vs conventional telephone instruction in cardiopulmonary resuscitation: the TACTIC cluster randomized trial
papers.summary: Cluster-randomized trial of 108 OHCA patients compared video-assisted dispatcher CPR instruction with conventional telephone instruction, finding no difference in bystander CPR rates (87.3% vs 92.5%, p=0.53) or ongoing CPR at EMS arrival, but significantly lower protocol compliance in the telemedicine group.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Pragmatic pilot cluster-randomised controlled trial
papers.n: 108 adults with non-traumatic OHCA (55 TA-CPR, 53 DA-CPR)
papers.finding: Bystander CPR rate 87.3% (TA-CPR) vs 92.5% (DA-CPR), p=0.53; ongoing CPR at EMS arrival 76.4% vs 84.9%, p=0.33. Protocol compliance significantly lower in TA-CPR (69.1% vs 92.5%).
papers.caveat: Small pilot with imbalanced baseline characteristics (younger patients, more shockable rhythms in TA-CPR) and limited power.
papers.shortTitle: Video dispatcher CPR no better than phone

papers.title: The AI dispatcher copilot: beyond cardiac arrest recognition to dynamic large language model-assisted Tele-CPR
papers.summary: Concept paper proposes an AI dispatcher copilot using multimodal large language models for dynamic Tele-CPR, integrating acoustic agonal breathing detection, adaptive instruction generation, real-time video CPR coaching with compression feedback, and automated first responder and AED coordination.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Narrative synthesis / concept paper
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Proposes an LLM-enabled 'AI dispatcher copilot' integrating agonal breathing detection, adaptive instruction generation, video CPR coaching and automated first responder/AED coordination, aligned with ERC 2025 guidelines.
papers.caveat: Purely conceptual with no patient data; requires prospective validation and ethical governance before use.
papers.shortTitle: AI dispatcher copilot concept for Tele-CPR

papers.title: Commentary
papers.summary: Commentary reinforcing that infection control standards must be maintained for all percutaneous procedures including those perceived as routine like POCUS-guided cannulation, following widespread adoption of point-of-care ultrasound.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Commentary on infection control standards for percutaneous procedures
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Infection control standards must be maintained for all percutaneous procedures, including routine POCUS-guided cannulation; no outcome numbers reported
papers.caveat: Commentary without original data
papers.shortTitle: Keep infection control for POCUS procedures

papers.title: Deciphering mitochondrial therapeutic heterogeneity at the post-resuscitation point of care
papers.summary: No abstract available — title suggests exploration of mitochondrial-directed therapies after return of spontaneous circulation.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.shortTitle: Mitochondrial therapies after ROSC

papers.title: Known to crews, missing from the literature - electrostatic discharge during helicopter hoist operations
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Editorial summarising two nationwide Norwegian studies demonstrating electrostatic discharge affects all rescue paramedics and 73% of physicians, with 23% experiencing severe events including pain, falls, impaired communication, and operation termination.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.shortTitle: Electrostatic discharge in helicopter hoists

papers.title: Evaluating performance and potential clinical benefit of the Swedish On Scene Injury Severity Prediction (OSISP) model for prehospital field triage on Norwegian trauma data
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: External validation of AI-based trauma triage model on 29,709 Norwegian trauma patients showed OSISP combined with clinical judgement reduced undertriage from 56% to 2.7% and mortality from 4.1% to 3.4–3.5%.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: External validation of prediction model on national trauma registry data
papers.n: 29,709 adult trauma patients attended by EMS in Norway, 2017–2022
papers.finding: OSISP alone: AUC ROC 0.83, undertriage 5.0%, overtriage 61.0%. Combined with existing triage: undertriage reduced from 56.0% to 2.7% and overtriage from 30.6% to 19.7%; estimated mortality reduction from 4.1% to 3.4–3.5%
papers.caveat: External validation in Norwegian registry data; mortality benefit modelled, not demonstrated prospectively
papers.shortTitle: AI trauma triage model validated in Norway

papers.title: Reply to: Sex-specific effects of manual pressure augmentation during defibrillation: a mechanistic hypothesis
papers.summary: Author response to criticism of sex-specific findings in the DOSE VF trial, defending the methodology and arguing biological plausibility for differential effects of manual pressure augmentation.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.shortTitle: Sex-specific defibrillation findings defended

papers.title: Meta-heuristics for the maximal covering location problem with distance constraint. An application to ambulance location in Spanish rural areas
papers.journal: Operations Research, Data Analytics and Logistics
papers.summary: Mathematical optimisation study applying meta-heuristic algorithms to ambulance station location problems in rural Spain, focusing on maximising population coverage within distance constraints.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.shortTitle: Optimising ambulance locations in rural Spain

papers.title: Comparison of burn surface area estimated by ambulance crews or referring hospitals and an Advanced Critical Care and Emergency Center
papers.summary: Study comparing burn size estimates by ambulance crews and referring hospitals against definitive assessment at a specialised burn center — reports accuracy of prehospital burn assessment.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre comparison
papers.n: 176 burn inpatients (134 direct ambulance transport, 42 inter-hospital transfer), Japan
papers.finding: Pre-transfer burn surface area estimates by ambulance crews and referring physicians exceeded specialist assessments but the overestimation was not clinically important
papers.caveat: Single Japanese centre; generalisability limited
papers.shortTitle: Ambulance crews estimate burn size accurately

papers.title: Prehospital epinephrine as a bridge to survival in traumatic cardiac arrest: A nationwide propensity score-matched analysis
papers.journal: The American Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Prehospital epinephrine administration in patients with traumatic cardiac arrest was associated with increased survival to hospital discharge and prehospital ROSC.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Nationwide registry propensity score-matched analysis
papers.n: 22,105 adult traumatic OHCA patients; 807 matched pairs analysed
papers.finding: Prehospital adrenaline associated with higher survival to discharge (5.1% vs 2.6%, adjusted OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.36-1.39) and prehospital ROSC (12.8% vs 4.5%, adjusted OR 3.63, 95% CI 2.39-5.51); favourable neurological outcome only after adjustment (OR 1.11)
papers.caveat: Korean registry, very few patients received adrenaline (3.7%); retrospective design cannot establish causality
papers.shortTitle: Adrenaline in traumatic cardiac arrest survival

papers.title: Simulation-based dynamic optimization for ambulance dispatch and casualty distribution in mass casualty incident
papers.summary: Study on: Simulation-based dynamic optimization for ambulance dispatch and casualty distribution in mass casualty incident. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.shortTitle: Simulation optimisation for MCI ambulance dispatch

papers.title: Prehospital pelvic binder use and transfusion requirements in patients with pelvic fractures: A nationwide propensity-matched cohort study
papers.summary: In this nationwide propensity-matched cohort of patients with blunt pelvic fractures, prehospital pelvic binder use was not associated with reduced 24-hour transfusion requirements or in-hospital mortality, but was associated with a higher rate of pelvic angioembolization.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective nationwide registry cohort with propensity matching
papers.n: 10,332 adults with blunt pelvic fractures; 182 binder users vs 546 matched controls
papers.finding: No difference in 24-hour RBC transfusion (median 2.0 vs 0.0 units; P=0.486) or in-hospital mortality; binder use associated with higher pelvic angioembolisation rate (33.0% vs 21.2%; OR 1.82, 95% CI 1.24-2.66)
papers.caveat: Only 1.8% received prehospital binders, suggesting selection and confounding by indication despite matching; Japanese system
papers.shortTitle: Prehospital pelvic binders don't cut transfusion

papers.title: Pilot evaluation of smart glasses for communication workflow and task performance in prehospital care
papers.summary: Smart glasses have the potential to enhance EMS-OLMC communication and improve completion of physician-guided critical tasks, though these benefits come with longer interactions.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Pilot randomised crossover simulation trial
papers.n: 16 simulated EMS sessions across two US agencies
papers.finding: Smart glasses improved completion of physician-guided critical tasks but significantly lengthened simulation and teleconsultation durations compared with phone (p<0.05)
papers.caveat: Small pilot simulation study, no patient outcomes
papers.shortTitle: Smart glasses for EMS–physician communication

papers.title: Mean airway pressure as the missing link in CPR physiology: A prehospital comparison of manual and mechanical chest compressions
papers.journal: The American Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Prehospital mPAW values were substantially lower than those reported in previous ED-based studies.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Prospective exploratory pilot observational study
papers.n: 19 adults with OHCA (10 manual, 9 mechanical compressions)
papers.finding: Median initial mean airway pressure was 7.74 mbar; higher early with mechanical (8.96 vs 6.54 mbar); ROSC patients had higher mPAW but not statistically significant
papers.caveat: Very small sample, single Belgian service, exploratory
papers.shortTitle: Airway pressures during manual vs mechanical CPR

papers.title: Psychosocial predictors of mental health outcomes in different groups of emergency responders: implications for tailored support systems
papers.summary: This study provides important insights into the mental health challenges faced by emergency service workers (ESWs), including paramedics, firefighters, and emergency medical dispatchers (EMDs).
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Cross-sectional survey with regression analysis
papers.n: 686 trainee paramedics, firefighters and EMDs from three Australian organisations
papers.finding: Higher resilience correlated with fewer symptoms (depression β=-.28, anxiety β=-.28, stress β=-.27, all p<.001); social support predicted depression (β=-.19); in EMDs trauma exposure predicted somatic symptoms (β=.22)
papers.caveat: Cross-sectional trainee sample, cannot establish causality
papers.shortTitle: Resilience predicts paramedic mental health symptoms

papers.title: The impact of an ambulance destination policy change on emergency department care metrics in New York City
papers.journal: The American Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: EMS destination policies can affect ED care delivery metrics.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective multicentre before-after study
papers.n: 943,658 ED visits across NYC Health + Hospitals (481,260 pre; 462,398 post)
papers.finding: Time-to-clinician fell 16.4% (15 to 12 min), ED length of stay fell 1% (151 to 149 min), LWBS fell from 0.9% to 0.7%, daily volume fell from 286 to 275; boarding unchanged
papers.caveat: Before-after design, US setting, cannot isolate policy from other temporal changes
papers.shortTitle: Nearest-hospital transport policy affects ED metrics

papers.title: Effectiveness of Multidisciplinary “Case Management” Approaches to the Management of Patients Who Make High Use of the Emergency Ambulance Service: A Quasi-experimental Evaluation Using Linked Routine Records
papers.summary: Study on: Effectiveness of Multidisciplinary “Case Management” Approaches to the Management of Patients Who Make High Use of the Emergency Ambulance Service: A Quasi-experimental Evaluation Using Linked Routine. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Quasi-experimental retrospective linked-routine-records cohort
papers.n: 1,183 high-use patients across 4 UK ambulance services (550 case management, 633 usual care)
papers.finding: No difference in death or any emergency health contact within 6 months (95.6% vs 94.9%; adjusted OR 1.159, 95% CI 0.595-2.255); 6-month mortality 10.5% vs 14.1%
papers.caveat: Natural experiment without randomisation; high baseline contact rates limit ability to detect differences
papers.shortTitle: Case management for high ambulance users ineffective

papers.title: Systemic Inefficiency versus Geographic Proximity: Decoupling Distance from Prehospital Delay in Urban Interhospital Trauma Transfers, Guayaquil-Ecuador
papers.summary: Prehospital delay and injury severity exhibit a lethal synergistic interaction.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre cohort with regression modelling
papers.n: 339 trauma patients in Guayaquil, Ecuador (274 in main analysis)
papers.finding: Prehospital delay predicted complications (RR 1.55, 95% CI 1.01-2.38); significant time × severity interaction (P=0.003); mortality escalated for critical patients after the first hour; transport distance did not differ between early and delayed groups (P=0.226)
papers.caveat: Retrospective single-city study, predominantly penetrating trauma, fragmented LMIC system limits generalisability
papers.shortTitle: Referral delays, not distance, drive trauma deaths

papers.title: Prehospital prediction of mechanical circulatory support during hospital stay in cardiogenic shock: The FLAG score
papers.summary: The FLAG risk score is a simple, registry-based model to predict MCS treatment during hospital stay in a prehospital setting.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective registry-based risk score development study
papers.n: 431 prehospital patients with cardiogenic shock at two German university hospitals
papers.finding: MCS implanted in 34.3%; FLAG score (fibrinolysis, CPR ≥35 min, age ≥65, female) predicted MCS with AUROC 0.707 in internal validation; predicted risk 16.9% to 83.1%
papers.caveat: Retrospective derivation with only internal validation, modest AUROC, no external validation
papers.shortTitle: FLAG score predicts circulatory support need in shock

papers.title: Sex differences in OHCA outcomes are driven by arrest circumstances rather than different EMS treatment: a nationwide registry study from Norway 2015 to 2024
papers.summary: We found differences in baseline characteristics and treatment performed by Emergency Medical Services (EMS) between women and men, as well as differences in survived event and survival to 30 days.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective 10-year national registry cohort with multivariable regression
papers.n: 27,621 EMS-treated OHCA cases (32% women)
papers.finding: Women had higher odds of survived event (adjusted) but lower 30-day survival; treatment differences did not appear sex-related, and sex differences in survival were unexplained by included variables
papers.caveat: Retrospective registry data; residual confounding — survival differences remained unexplained
papers.shortTitle: Sex differences in OHCA survival, Norwegian registry

papers.title: Ketamine Versus Propofol for Sedation in Acute Psychiatric Emergencies During Aeromedical Retrieval: A Randomized Clinical Trial
papers.summary: In this RCT of 170 patients, ketamine was associated with fewer adverse events compared to propofol when used for sedation during aeromedical retrieval of patients experiencing acute psychiatric agitation.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Prospective single-centre open-label randomised controlled trial
papers.n: 170 agitated patients undergoing aeromedical retrieval
papers.finding: Adverse events 12.4% with ketamine vs 24.7% with propofol (RR 0.50, 95% CI 0.25-0.99, p=0.039); similar efficacy reaching target RASS (OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.50-1.07); clinicians preferred propofol
papers.caveat: Stopped early due to low enrolment; open-label single-centre design
papers.shortTitle: Ketamine vs propofol for aeromedical psychiatric sedation

papers.title: Characterizing Pediatric Trauma Patients and EMS Agencies That Are Optimal Targets for Prehospital Pediatric Blood Transfusion Programs
papers.summary: In a nationally representative prehospital sample, many injured children appeared eligible for transfusion.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective analysis of national prehospital registry data
papers.n: 2,492,731 paediatric encounters; 34,221 potentially transfusion-eligible
papers.finding: 1.37% of encounters met physiological transfusion criteria; blood was given in 669 encounters overall and to 1.01% of eligible children; only 240/16,848 (1.4%) agencies provided blood to children
papers.caveat: US registry data with physiological proxy criteria; potential misclassification of eligibility
papers.shortTitle: Which paediatric trauma cases warrant prehospital blood

papers.title: Prehospital Assessment and Treatment of Infants and Toddlers in Respiratory Distress: A Retrospective Analysis
papers.summary: EMS clinicians documented similar primary impressions and administered many of the same treatments across both upper and lower airway groups, demonstrating minimal differentiation in prehospital management of young children.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective analysis of linked prehospital and ED records
papers.n: 1,352 children under 3 years (346 upper airway)
papers.finding: 'Acute respiratory distress' was the commonest EMS impression in both groups (60.4% upper, 50.0% lower); EtCO2 recorded in only 8%; treatments overlapped and often did not align with final ED diagnosis
