papers.finding: CT use rose from 32 to 44 per 100 ED presentations before go-live, then declined 9.1% during clinician engagement phase; trends stabilised after eCDS deployment
papers.caveat: Single-centre descriptive design without control group; cannot attribute causation
papers.shortTitle: Decision support for ED imaging referrals

papers.title: What Is Old Is New Again: Tips and Tricks for Recognizing and Treating Vaccine‐Preventable Diseases of Childhood Presenting to the Emergency Department
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Across the globe, there has been a resurgence in vaccine‐preventable diseases reflecting declining immunity, vaccine hesitancy and gaps in vaccine coverage.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.design: Narrative review/overview
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Highlights resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases such as measles and diphtheria and the need for emergency clinicians to recognise and manage them
papers.caveat: Narrative overview without systematic methods or original data
papers.shortTitle: Vaccine-preventable diseases in the ED

papers.title: Management of Adult Closed Head Injury in Rural Queensland Without Hospital‐Based CT : A Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.summary: Patients with closed head injury in this rural emergency department had substantial neuroimaging needs despite the absence of hospital‐based CT.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre cohort
papers.n: 118 adults with closed head injury at Dalby Hospital, Queensland
papers.finding: 50.8% underwent CT (half offsite private, half via interhospital transfer); intracranial haemorrhage in 15.0% of imaged patients; documented observation in 46.6%; driving advice documented in only 6.9% of discharged patients
papers.caveat: Small single-site sample with retrospective manual record review; documentation may undercount care given
papers.shortTitle: Rural head injury care without on-site CT

papers.title: Initial Laryngoscope Blade Selection and Outcomes in Paediatric Emergency Department Intubations: Miller vs. Macintosh
papers.summary: In this cohort of young children intubated in the ED, Macintosh blade use was associated with higher FPS and fewer hypoxic events compared with Miller blade.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Prospectively collected registry cohort (ANZEDAR)
papers.n: 201 children under 5 intubated in ED
papers.finding: Macintosh blades had higher FPS (80.5% vs 63.6%; OR 0.42, 95% CI 0.22–0.80) and lower hypoxia (17.7% vs 33.0%; OR 2.28, 95% CI 1.19–4.46) than Miller; hypotension rates did not differ
papers.caveat: Miller-blade children were substantially younger, making age a significant confounder; in-hospital ED setting
papers.shortTitle: Miller vs Macintosh blade in paediatric intubation

papers.title: The Return of Diphtheria: Reflections From the Emergency Department
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Diphtheria has re‐emerged in Australia in 2026, prompting significant public health concern and placing additional demands on healthcare services.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Descriptive review of diphtheria outbreak impact on EDs
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Diphtheria disproportionately affected Indigenous communities; ED challenges included case identification, rapid guideline development, broader cutaneous presentations and workforce strain from contact tracing and staff isolation
papers.caveat: Descriptive commentary without quantitative outcome data
papers.shortTitle: Diphtheria re-emergence and ED impact

papers.title: Caregiver and Care Recipient Perspectives on Paediatric ED Mental Health Presentations: A Qualitative Study
papers.summary: Care recipients and care providers identified challenges in service coordination, clinician readiness and the ED environment.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Secondary qualitative analysis of Delphi free-text responses (PREDICT network)
papers.n: 184 participants (36 care recipients, 148 care providers) across 12 EDs and pre-hospital services in Australia
papers.finding: Three main themes: care continuity and communication gaps, ED environment challenges, and need for improved training, behavioural support, reduced sensory overload and community care links
papers.caveat: Secondary analysis of free-text Delphi responses, not purpose-designed interviews; self-selected respondents
papers.shortTitle: Perspectives on paediatric ED mental health care

papers.title: Epidemiology of Patients With Chronic Liver Disease Presenting to Emergency Departments in Australia
papers.summary: CLD‐related ED presentations are increasing and place substantial demand on hospital services in Queensland.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Statewide data linkage cohort
papers.n: 23,578 CLD-related ED presentations involving 11,961 adults across 104 Queensland EDs
papers.finding: CLD presentations rose 2% annually (IRR 1.02, 95% CI 1.02–1.03); 86.1% admitted, 4.5% to ICU, 4.1% in-hospital death; predictors of 30-day mortality included cirrhosis (aHR 6.92), malignancy (aHR 3.21) and hepatorenal syndrome (aHR 3.15); tertiary hospital presentation had lower mortality (aHR 0.75, 95% CI 0.68–0.82)
papers.caveat: Retrospective linked administrative data; Queensland-only; residual confounding likely
papers.shortTitle: Chronic liver disease ED presentations in Queensland

papers.title: Exploring Inter‐Rater Agreement in Classification of Radiological Features of Tension in Adults With Primary Spontaneous Pneumothorax
papers.summary: Interpretation for radiological tension features had poor inter‐rater reliability, which seriously changes their appropriateness as drivers for interventional management.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.design: Blinded observational inter-rater agreement study
papers.n: Five emergency physicians reviewing 80 PSP chest x-rays
papers.finding: Inter-rater agreement for radiological tension features was Krippendorff's Alpha 0.524 (95% CI 0.400–0.623), indicating poor agreement
papers.caveat: Small number of x-rays and reviewers; in-hospital ED setting
papers.shortTitle: Poor agreement on radiological tension features

papers.title: Timing and outcomes of out-of-hospital traumatic cardiac arrest: results of a multicentre, retrospective cohort study
papers.summary: Nine out of ten out-of-hospital TCAs occur before EMS arrival.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Multicentre retrospective observational cohort (nationwide HEMS)
papers.n: 1,532 patients with out-of-hospital traumatic cardiac arrest
papers.finding: 90.2% sustained TCA before EMS arrival, 8.2% after EMS arrival and 1.6% during HEMS transport; sustained ROSC occurred in 20.8%, 47.2% and 92.0% respectively; meaningful survival achievable regardless of TCA onset
papers.caveat: Retrospective design; HEMS-attended patients only, limiting generalisability to routine ambulance responses
papers.shortTitle: Timing of out-of-hospital traumatic cardiac arrest

papers.title: Consistency of definitions used in International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Neonatal Life Support documents
papers.summary: Study on: Consistency of definitions used in International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation Neonatal Life Support documents. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Structured review of ILCOR Neonatal Life Support Task Force documents
papers.n: 227 unique terms extracted from 67 documents; 63 terms assessed for consistency
papers.finding: Only 23 of 63 terms (37%) had similar definitions across documents; the rest were inconsistent or used different terms for similar constructs
papers.caveat: Terminology analysis only, no clinical outcomes
papers.shortTitle: Inconsistent definitions in neonatal ILCOR documents

papers.title: Automated External Defibrillator pad placement pictograms in Japan: sex representation in publicly available product information
papers.summary: Study on: Automated External Defibrillator pad placement pictograms in Japan: sex representation in publicly available product information. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.shortTitle: AED pad pictograms and sex representation in Japan

papers.title: Public Access Defibrillation by Activated Community First Responders - the randomized HeartRunner Trial
papers.summary: Study on: Public Access Defibrillation by Activated Community First Responders - the randomized HeartRunner Trial. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.design: Investigator-initiated randomised controlled trial (protocol paper)
papers.n: 15,401 registered community first responders in a Danish region of ~1.9 million; planned randomisation of 4,188 suspected OHCA cases
papers.caveat: Protocol paper; results not yet available (trial due to complete February 2026)
papers.shortTitle: Smartphone-dispatched community responders in OHCA

papers.title: Step-by-step: Translating deliberate practice to the bedside
papers.summary: Study on: Step-by-step: Translating deliberate practice to the bedside. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.shortTitle: Deliberate practice translated to bedside

papers.title: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation with synchronized ventilation versus 3:1 compression to ventilation ratio in a neonatal porcine model
papers.summary: In a neonatal piglet model of asystolic cardiac arrest, CCSV resulted in a significantly faster time to ROSC compared to 3:1 C:V.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Randomised animal experimental study
papers.n: 16 neonatal piglets (1-3 days old, 1.8-2.5 kg)
papers.finding: Median time to ROSC 61 s (IQR 51-118) with chest compression synchronised ventilation vs 170 s (IQR 105-312) with 3:1 C:V (p=0.030); ROSC rate 7/8 vs 5/8 (p=1.000)
papers.caveat: Small animal (porcine) model; findings may not translate to human neonatal resuscitation
papers.shortTitle: Synchronised ventilation faster ROSC in neonatal piglets

papers.title: Strengthening workplace emergency preparedness through a university CPR and first aid responder programme: four-year experience
papers.summary: Study on: Strengthening workplace emergency preparedness through a university CPR and first aid responder programme: four-year experience. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.design: Four-year programme evaluation with feedback questionnaire
papers.n: 84 workplace first aid responder respondents
papers.finding: High self-reported confidence in CPR (mean 5.11 ± 1.00) and AED use (5.22 ± 0.98); 23.8% and 35.7% encountered workplace and non-workplace emergencies respectively, and all provided assistance
papers.caveat: Self-reported perceptions from a single university setting; small sample, no objective performance data
papers.shortTitle: University first aid programme boosts preparedness

papers.title: Conservative versus liberal oxygen therapy in hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy following cardiac arrest: a trial-based cost-effectiveness analysis
papers.summary: Conservative oxygen was associated with modest cost savings and small differences in health outcomes, with no clear economic advantage over liberal oxygen.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Trial-based cost-effectiveness analysis alongside the LOGICAL RCT
papers.n: 1,821 critically ill adults with post-cardiac arrest hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy across 53 ICUs in Australia, NZ and Ireland
papers.finding: Conservative oxygen: incremental cost -$1,392 (95% CI -$4,696 to $1,911), favourable functional outcome 38.2% (risk difference -1.5 percentage points, 95% CI -6.1 to 3.2), incremental QALYs -0.002 (95% CI -0.013 to 0.008); no clear economic advantage
papers.caveat: In-hospital ICU population; health system perspective, cost estimates may not generalise
papers.shortTitle: Cost-effectiveness of conservative oxygen post-arrest

papers.title: Comparing Chest compression Quality in 1-Minute vs. 2-Minute Rescuer Rotations with and without Audiovisual Feedback Guidance during full Adult Advance Life Support Simulated Scenarios: A Randomized Simulation Study
papers.summary: Study on: Comparing Chest compression Quality in 1-Minute vs. 2-Minute Rescuer Rotations with and without Audiovisual Feedback Guidance during full Adult Advance Life Support Simulated Scenarios: A Randomized S. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.design: Randomised simulation study (four groups, 2x2 factorial)
papers.n: 31 participants; 30 compressors' data per group across 10 simulated CPR sessions per group
papers.finding: Audiovisual feedback improved compression depth and in-target performance (median in-target 9.7% vs 52.8% in 1-min groups; p<0.05); 1-min rotations had lower chest compression fraction; 2-min rotation with feedback performed best overall
papers.caveat: Manikin simulation only; small sample; findings may not translate to real resuscitation
papers.shortTitle: 1 vs 2-minute compressor rotation with feedback

papers.title: Beyond feasibility: does simulation-based POCUS training translate into clinically meaningful pediatric arrest performance?
papers.summary: Study on: Beyond feasibility: does simulation-based POCUS training translate into clinically meaningful pediatric arrest performance?. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.shortTitle: Simulation POCUS training in paediatric arrest

papers.title: Validation of a Hospital-Wide Risk Stratification Model for Predicting Code Events Among Critically Ill Children
papers.summary: Study on: Validation of a Hospital-Wide Risk Stratification Model for Predicting Code Events Among Critically Ill Children. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.design: Single-centre retrospective external validation study (2020-2023)
papers.n: 5,254 paediatric encounters, of which 2.6% had at least one code event
papers.finding: pCREST predicted code events within 12 h with c-statistic 0.80; 13-fold improvement in detection over outcome prevalence; high performance up to 18 h pre-event; transfer learning did not improve performance
papers.caveat: Single-centre retrospective validation; in-hospital PICU setting with low event rate (precision-recall curve 0.034)
papers.shortTitle: Machine learning predicts paediatric code events

papers.title: External Validation and Comparative Performance of ACLS, SARICA, NULL-PLEASE, BDR scores for In-Hospital Mortality after Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.summary: Study on: External Validation and Comparative Performance of ACLS, SARICA, NULL-PLEASE, BDR scores for In-Hospital Mortality after Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective multicentre cohort (external validation)
papers.n: 1036 adults with OHCA and ROSC
papers.finding: 718 (69.3%) died in hospital. BDR score had best discrimination (AUROC 0.775; 95% CI 0.745-0.805), followed by NULL-PLEASE (0.756), modified SARICA (0.746) and modified ACLS (0.662); BDR, NULL-PLEASE and SARICA all outperformed ACLS. Specificity only moderate at Youden thresholds.
papers.caveat: Patients missing CT, blood gas or lactate data excluded, risking selection bias; retrospective design and moderate specificity limit clinical use.
papers.shortTitle: BDR best score for post-OHCA mortality

papers.title: Characteristics of pediatric drowning out-of-hospital cardiac arrests in the United States
papers.summary: Study on: Characteristics of pediatric drowning out-of-hospital cardiac arrests in the United States. No abstract available for detailed assessment.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Cross-sectional analysis of national EMS registry
papers.n: 753 drowning-related paediatric OHCAs (1 day-17 years)
papers.finding: Most were toddlers 1-4 years (57.8%), male (64.5%), at private residences (72.5%) and urban (83.7%); 73.7% unwitnessed, 81.3% received bystander CPR. Adolescent arrests were more often witnessed and more likely to achieve ROSC.
papers.caveat: Descriptive US registry data with incomplete outcome reporting; results may not translate to the Australian prehospital system.
papers.shortTitle: US paediatric drowning OHCA characteristics

papers.title: Improving surgical team confidence for intraoperative cardiac arrest in non-standard positions (sitting beach chair and prone): a prospective in-situ simulation study with three-month follow-up
papers.summary: A half-day, multi-station in situ simulation course at an elective surgical unit was associated with higher self-reported confidence at three months, and self-reported application of course content to real patients.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Prospective single-centre in-situ simulation educational study with 3-month follow-up
papers.n: 63 interprofessional surgical staff in five teams
papers.finding: Self-reported confidence higher at three months in all four domains (p<0.05; effect sizes r 0.39-0.68); 48/56 (85.7%) reported course content useful for a real patient. Repositioning transfers took ~35 s (sitting to supine) and ~30 s (prone to supine).
papers.caveat: Single-centre, uncontrolled design with self-reported outcomes and varied questionnaire response rates (74-92%); in-hospital surgical setting.
papers.shortTitle: Simulation builds team confidence for prone/beach-chair arrest

papers.title: Effects of tocilizumab on neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, and its prognostic value
papers.summary: Tocilizumab did not affect NGAL in comatose survivors of OHCA.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Substudy of the IMICA randomised controlled trial
papers.n: 80 comatose adult OHCA survivors
papers.finding: NGAL levels 0-72 h did not differ between tocilizumab and placebo. Admission NGAL predicted cRRT need (AUROC 0.76) and 180-day death (AUROC 0.75; significantly better than creatinine, AUROC 0.54).
papers.caveat: Small substudy sample and null secondary biomarker endpoints limit precision and generalisability.
papers.shortTitle: Tocilizumab no effect on NGAL after OHCA

papers.title: Public defibrillators: high investment, low return – lowering the cost per shock – the D€FI-CO$T study
papers.summary: Analysis of public AED deployment cost-effectiveness found very low usage rates relative to investment — the study examines strategies to improve cost per delivered shock.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.shortTitle: Public AED cost per shock

papers.title: Resolving uncertainties in patient selection for mechanical circulatory support after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
papers.summary: Review of patient selection criteria for ECPR after OHCA.
