papers.shortTitle: Selecting patients for ECPR after OHCA

papers.title: Late Tranexamic Acid After Trauma: Uncertainty Is Not Neutral
papers.summary: Commentary on the evidence gap around TXA administration beyond 3 hours post-injury.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.shortTitle: Late TXA after trauma: uncertainty

papers.title: Early Intensive Blood Pressure Reduction After Intracerebral Hemorrhage Is Associated With Worse Functional Outcome: The Risk of Overshooting Blood Pressure Goals
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort examining whether rapid systolic BP reduction ≤150 mm Hg after spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage improved outcomes — early target achievement and overshooting <120 mm Hg were associated with worse functional outcome.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.shortTitle: Over-rapid BP drop worse after ICH

papers.title: Maintenance of prehospital anaesthesia using an intermittent bolus regime in blunt trauma patients with a high GCS and hemodynamic reserve: a retrospective cohort study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Retrospective study showing that prehospital anaesthesia maintenance using intermittent boluses results in high variability of cumulative sedative/analgesic doses, potentially risking sub-therapeutic plasma levels.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Single-centre retrospective observational study at a UK HEMS
papers.n: 101 blunt trauma patients with GCS ≥9 undergoing prehospital anaesthesia
papers.finding: Median prehospital anaesthetic duration 56 min; maintenance doses highly variable (fentanyl 0.64 [0-1.41] mcg/kg/h; midazolam 0.028 [0-0.041] mg/kg/h); 8 patients received no maintenance sedation or analgesia
papers.caveat: Retrospective, single-centre, homogeneous low-risk cohort; surrogate dosing measures only, no plasma levels measured
papers.shortTitle: Bolus-only prehospital RSI maintenance highly variable

papers.title: Combined short- and mid-latency SSEP amplitudes for early prediction of favorable neurological recovery after cardiac arrest
papers.summary: They tested whether combined somatosensory evoked potential amplitudes could predict favorable neurological recovery after cardiac arrest and found the combined measure outperformed traditional single-latency assessments.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective cohort
papers.n: 73 comatose adult cardiac arrest patients post-ROSC with SSEP within 24 h
papers.finding: 29 (40%) had favourable 6-month outcome; P25-N30 amplitude AUC 0.943 (95% CI 0.862-0.984), 100% sensitivity and 84.1% specificity
papers.caveat: Very small single-centre retrospective sample
papers.shortTitle: SSEP amplitudes predict good arrest recovery

papers.title: Naloxone administration associated with improved survival in PEA out-of-hospital cardiac arrests
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort (n=40,333) testing whether prehospital naloxone improves outcomes stratified by presenting rhythm, and found naloxone was associated with higher survival to discharge in PEA arrests but not in shockable rhythms or asystole.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective cohort with propensity-score matching
papers.n: 40,333 OHCA cases; 7,567 (18.8%) received naloxone
papers.finding: In PEA arrests, naloxone was associated with higher survival to discharge (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.11-1.92) but not ROSC (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.90-1.31); no association in shockable rhythms or asystole
papers.caveat: Retrospective design; selection bias and resuscitation time bias not fully addressed, causality unproven
papers.shortTitle: Naloxone linked to better PEA arrest survival

papers.title: Best practices on blood and blood products for a prehospital hemorrhage protocol: consensus from the 2025 Canadian prehospital transfusion summit
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Consensus summit with 50+ experts developed 12 statements on prehospital transfusion, identifying RBCs and TXA as foundational, recommending freeze-dried plasma and whole blood for rural settings, and emphasising calcium and hypothermia prevention.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Structured roundtable consensus summit
papers.n: Over 50 experts from eight provinces and six services/systems
papers.finding: 12 consensus statements: red blood cells and tranexamic acid foundational; freeze-dried plasma and whole blood favoured in rural/remote settings; calcium and hypothermia prevention essential
papers.caveat: Expert opinion consensus rather than direct evidence; Canadian context
papers.shortTitle: Canadian consensus on prehospital transfusion

papers.title: Identification and Documentation of Patient Social Risk Factors in the Prehospital Setting: A Pilot Implementation
papers.summary: This pilot implementation tested whether EMS clinicians can reliably identify and document patient social risk factors during routine care, finding that structured documentation is feasible but requires workflow integration and clinician training.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective cohort of charted encounters after implementing a required 14-item social risk factor documentation tool
papers.n: 57,899 adult EMS encounters
papers.finding: Only 4.0% of encounters (n = 2,326) had a documented social risk factor; most common were substance use (31.3%), housing instability (25.7%) and disability (25.4%); >75% of encounters were low acuity.
papers.caveat: Single agency pilot; low documentation rate may reflect screening or workflow barriers rather than true prevalence
papers.shortTitle: Documenting social risk factors in EMS charts

papers.title: External Validation of the SCARE Score for Predicting Acute Myocardial Infarction in Patients Calling Emergency Medical Communication Centers: A Prospective Multicenter Study
papers.summary: They prospectively validated the SCARE score for predicting acute myocardial infarction during telephone triage across multiple French emergency communication centers, finding good discrimination and calibration but noting limitations in real-world implementation.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Prospective multicentre observational validation cohort
papers.n: 2,042 adults hospitalised after EMCC calls for non-traumatic chest pain
papers.finding: 265 (13.0%) had AMI; SCARE AUROC 0.85 (95% CI 0.82-0.87), AUROC 0.84 in men and 0.89 in women; at >35 points sensitivity 73.6%, specificity 75.3%, NPV 95.0%
papers.caveat: Score not used in real time and did not influence dispatch; French physician-staffed dispatch centres, so applicability to non-physician dispatch systems untested
papers.shortTitle: SCARE score validates for chest pain triage

papers.title: Large Language Models Exhibit High Performance as Computable Phenotypes for Pediatric Asthma Exacerbation Detection in a Retrospective, Observational Study of Emergency Medical Services Encounters
papers.summary: They tested whether large language models could accurately identify paediatric asthma exacerbations from EMS documentation, finding high performance but noting this is early exploratory work with real-world deployment challenges.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective observational study of LLM computable phenotypes
papers.n: 24,283 EMS encounters, patients aged 2-18 years; 1,000 annotated encounters
papers.finding: Best model (Llama-3.3-70B, unstructured+structured data, 10-shot chain-of-thought) achieved F1 score 0.894; chain-of-thought prompts outperformed basic prompts in 4 of 5 models
papers.caveat: Early exploratory work; real-world deployment not tested
papers.shortTitle: LLMs identify paediatric asthma in EMS data

papers.title: Service Ready Ambulance Surfaces and Emergency Medical Services Clinicians are Routinely Contaminated with Clinically Important Pathogens
papers.summary: This study found that ambulance surfaces and clinicians remain contaminated with clinically important pathogens even after routine cleaning, suggesting current disinfection protocols may be inadequate to prevent healthcare-associated infections during patient transport.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Prospective observational study with pre- and post-shift sampling
papers.n: 20 ambulances and 27 EMS clinicians, 941 samples
papers.finding: 18.5% of samples harboured ≥1 clinically important pathogen (MSSA 12.8%, MRSA 4.6%, VRE 3.0%); when service ready, 60% of ambulances and 63.1% of clinicians had ≥1 pathogen, similar post-shift (60% and 67.6%).
papers.caveat: Small sample from only two US EMS agencies
papers.shortTitle: Ambulances and clinicians contaminated with pathogens

papers.title: Evaluation of the trauma criteria from the Norwegian national trauma plan: an observational study from a regional trauma centre
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: They tested whether Norway's new national trauma criteria accurately predicted ISS>15 injuries and met triage goals, and found overtriage of 81.1% and undertriage of 11.5%, with mechanism of injury criteria showing very poor positive predictive value.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective cohort from a regional trauma registry with manual prehospital record review
papers.n: 2,508 trauma registry patients, 384 with ISS >15
papers.finding: Overtriage 81.1%, undertriage 11.5%; mechanism-of-injury criteria predicted ISS >15 in only 9 of 333 patients (overtriage 97.3%); removing MOI criteria except fall would eliminate 255 unnecessary trauma team activations.
papers.caveat: Single trauma centre, Norwegian system; findings may not transfer to Australian triage criteria
papers.shortTitle: Norwegian trauma criteria: high overtriage

papers.title: Global inventory and audit of road injury data systems: a descriptive study using the Road Injury Chain of Survival Framework
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: They audited global road injury data systems to assess coverage across the Road Injury Chain of Survival, and found extensive fragmentation with few systems linking crash, rescue, prehospital, and hospital data, severely limiting quality improvement opportunities.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Descriptive global audit of national and regional road injury datasets against the Road Injury Chain of Survival framework
papers.n: 349 data systems (357 datasets) worldwide
papers.finding: Police crash databases most common; formal cross-sector data linkage rare; data coverage greatest for Early Recognition and substantially less for rescue, prehospital care, transport and hospital care links.
papers.caveat: Descriptive audit with unverified and aggregate-only datasets; coding subject to available documentation
papers.shortTitle: Road injury data systems highly fragmented

papers.title: Challenges faced by prehospital emergency physicians providing emergency care to pediatric patients
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: They surveyed emergency physicians and analysed 9,409 protocols to understand pediatric emergency preparedness, and found pediatric cases represent only 6.5% of prehospital physician deployments but physicians reported low confidence in neonatal care, intoxication, and pediatric polytrauma.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Mixed-methods: retrospective protocol analysis plus physician survey
papers.n: 9,409 prehospital physician protocols (606 paediatric cases) and 437 surveyed physicians
papers.finding: Paediatric cases were 6.45% of missions; high confidence for seizures, anaphylaxis and hypoglycaemia but markedly lower confidence for neonatal care, paediatric polytrauma and CPR; >70% supported mandatory simulation-based paediatric training.
papers.caveat: Self-perceived competence (not measured performance) and physician-staffed system not directly comparable to Australian paramedic practice
papers.shortTitle: Prehospital physicians underconfident in paediatrics

papers.title: Feasibility of Electric Vehicle Adoption in US Ambulance Fleets: A Retrospective Analysis of NEMSIS Data
papers.summary: Retrospective NEMSIS analysis examined operational feasibility of electric ambulance adoption — fleet integration appears viable under specific conditions, though infrastructure readiness remains key.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective analysis of NEMSIS 2024 data with modelling of EV ambulance ranges
papers.n: US 9-1-1 EMS calls from NEMSIS 2024 (number not stated)
papers.finding: Estimated mileage fell within EV range requirements for 97.6-99.9% of dispatches depending on urbanicity and vehicle capacity; at-hospital Level-2 and Level-3 charging restored significant fractions of energy used.
papers.caveat: Modelled hypothetical vehicle profiles rather than real-world EV ambulance operations
papers.shortTitle: Electric ambulances feasible in most dispatches

papers.title: Incidence of Adverse Events with Prehospital Use of Droperidol for Nausea or Vomiting
papers.summary: This study evaluated adverse events associated with prehospital droperidol use for nausea or vomiting — the incidence of clinically significant adverse events was low, suggesting droperidol may be safe for prehospital use.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective observational cohort, convenience sample
papers.n: 284 patients given prehospital droperidol for nausea/vomiting across 29 EMS agencies
papers.finding: 15.5% had at least one adverse event, most commonly decreased mentation (8.5%); hypoxia in 6.7% (mostly older adults, 13.2%); 90.1% received 1.25 mg; sedation incidence similar in older vs other adults.
papers.caveat: Convenience sample, retrospective design, and no comparison with other antiemetics
papers.shortTitle: Droperidol for nausea: low adverse event rate

papers.title: Effect of Compression Surfaces on Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Quality and Clinician Fatigue
papers.summary: They tested whether different compression surfaces affect CPR quality and clinician fatigue, and found surface characteristics significantly impact compression depth and rate consistency while also affecting provider fatigue.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Pilot randomised crossover manikin trial
papers.n: 40 EMS clinicians
papers.finding: Time to failure was 145 s (IQR 65–240) on floor vs 140 s (IQR 100–420) on mattress (p=0.64); compression rates 112/min vs 105/min (p=0.12); no difference in fatigue or compression quality between surfaces.
papers.caveat: Small pilot simulation study in young EMS clinicians; not powered for clinical outcomes
papers.shortTitle: CPR on mattress vs floor: similar fatigue

papers.title: Beyond blood pressure: The emerging role of wearable doppler ultrasound in prehospital care
papers.summary: They reviewed wearable Doppler ultrasound technology for prehospital haemodynamic monitoring, and found it may detect occult haemodynamic compromise earlier than standard vital signs alone.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Narrative review of wearable Doppler ultrasound technology
papers.n: Not reported
papers.shortTitle: Wearable Doppler ultrasound for prehospital monitoring

papers.title: Feasibility and challenges of large language model (LLM)-generated neonatal resuscitation simulations: a multicenter exploratory study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: This prospective multicenter pilot tested whether ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 could generate valid neonatal resuscitation simulation scenarios for training, finding ChatGPT-4o performed comparably to official NRP scenarios in overall quality while demonstrating strengths in debriefing design but having gaps in dynamic vital sign provision.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Prospective multicentre pilot study
papers.n: 16 simulation scenarios rated by 9 blinded instructors from 5 centres
papers.finding: ChatGPT-4o scenarios scored comparably to NRP® scenarios overall, with higher debriefing design scores (r=0.25, P=0.02); DeepSeek and RETAIN scored lower overall, and ChatGPT showed gaps in dynamic vital sign provision.
papers.caveat: Pilot study with only instructor ratings, no learner outcomes
papers.shortTitle: ChatGPT-4o generates neonatal resus scenarios

papers.title: Epidemiology and severity of mountain rescue missions in Poland: a retrospective study of 9,477 patients rescued by the Tatra Mountain Rescue Service
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Retrospective analysis of 9,477 mountain rescue missions over 10 years found a median NACA score of 2 with 38% classified as moderate-to-severe, seasonal variation in severity, and helicopter use correlated with higher acuity, providing epidemiological data that could inform training and resource planning for wilderness EMS.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected rescue registry data
papers.n: 9,477 patients rescued in the Polish Tatra Mountains 2015–2024
papers.finding: Median NACA score 2 (IQR 0–3); 38% NACA ≥3; deaths in 2%; median mission duration 1.75 h; ~24 rescues per 100,000 park visitors; severe cases more frequent in winter (6.3% vs 4.7%, p=0.001); helicopter use correlated with higher NACA scores.
papers.caveat: Single mountain rescue service in Poland; limited generalisability to Australian settings
papers.shortTitle: Tatra mountain rescue epidemiology over 10 years

papers.title: Design and rationale of a multicenter paramedic randomized trial of noradrenaline versus adrenaline in the initial management of patients with cardiogenic shock—The PANDA trial
papers.summary: This multicenter RCT protocol tests whether noradrenaline improves outcomes compared with adrenaline for paramedic management of cardiogenic shock, with the PANDA trial aiming to settle the debate on optimal vasopressor choice in the prehospital setting.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Protocol for prehospital multicentre open-label RCT
papers.n: Planned 1,155 patients with suspected cardiogenic shock (450 recruited to date)
papers.finding: Trial randomises paramedic-administered noradrenaline vs adrenaline to target SBP 100 mmHg; primary outcome 28-day all-cause mortality; results not yet available
papers.caveat: Protocol only — no outcome data yet
papers.shortTitle: PANDA trial: noradrenaline vs adrenaline in shock

papers.title: EMS protocol gaps for defibrillator pad placement in prehospital STEMI care
papers.journal: The American Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: They reviewed whether EMS protocols adequately address defibrillator pad placement in prehospital STEMI care, and found significant variability and gaps that may compromise monitoring and pacing capability during transport.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Cross-sectional review of state-wide EMS protocols
papers.n: 30 U.S. state-wide EMS protocols
papers.finding: Only 13% of protocols advised placing defibrillator pads on STEMI patients during transport, 17% suggested considering it, and 70% gave no guidance; 33% specified ECG acquisition timing and 67% emphasised early hospital notification.
papers.caveat: US protocols only, descriptive review without patient outcome data
papers.shortTitle: EMS protocols rarely guide pads in STEMI

papers.title: The Géocoeur system: recruiting real-time first responders at the point of the defibrillator
papers.summary: This study evaluated whether a geolocation system can recruit volunteer first responders to nearby defibrillators in real time, and found it successfully mobilised responders and shortened time to first shock compared with historical controls.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.shortTitle: Geolocation recruits responders to defibrillators

papers.title: From decision support to clinical integration: A scoping review of artificial intelligence in prehospital airway management
papers.summary: They reviewed AI applications in prehospital airway management and found most tools remain experimental, with limited integration into clinical workflows despite promising capabilities for difficult airway prediction and real-time guidance.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Scoping review (PRISMA-ScR)
papers.n: 9 studies published 2020–2026
papers.finding: AI applications spanned prediction/triage, physiological monitoring, documentation NLP, and computer vision for intubation; reported AUCs 0.867–0.960, but all studies used retrospective data with internal validation and none were prospective trials.
papers.caveat: Only nine small studies, all retrospective with limited external validation
papers.shortTitle: AI in prehospital airway care still experimental

papers.title: Impact of practical-based education on paramedic students' confidence and competence in assessing and managing mental health conditions
papers.summary: They tested whether practical-based education improved paramedic students' confidence and competence in mental health assessment and management, and found hands-on training significantly improved both self-efficacy and clinical performance compared with traditional classroom teaching.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective pre-post survey with OSCE scores
papers.n: 94 second-year paramedic students at an Australian university
papers.finding: Statistically significant increases in self-perceived confidence across assessment, communication, and management domains (p<0.05); confidence correlated with OSCE performance.
papers.caveat: Single-centre, self-reported confidence without control group; no long-term follow-up
papers.shortTitle: Practical education boosts mental health confidence

papers.title: Manufactured futility: prehospital system failure as the primary determinant of resuscitation outcomes in India
papers.summary: This commentary argues that poor resuscitation outcomes in India are driven by prehospital system failures rather than individual provider limitations, highlighting the need for structural reforms in emergency response infrastructure and training.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.shortTitle: System failure drives poor OHCA outcomes in India

papers.title: Racial and Geographic Disparities in Automated External Defibrillator Use During EMS Encounters in the United States
papers.summary: Analysis of AED deployment patterns during EMS encounters revealing racial and geographic differences in defibrillator access and application.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.design: Descriptive cross-sectional analysis of aggregated national EMS data
papers.n: 106,246 EMS encounters across six racial/ethnic groups
papers.finding: AED applied in 16,688 encounters (15.7%); rates varied by race and geography, with lowest use in White patients and markedly lower use in suburban and frontier areas
papers.caveat: Aggregated public data cannot distinguish true inequity from case or system factors
papers.shortTitle: AED use varies by race and geography

papers.title: Air or Ground EMS: The Fastest Route to Care in Alberta
papers.summary: Geospatial analysis comparing response and transport times for air versus ground EMS in Alberta to identify optimal triage criteria.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Geospatial multi-modal network modelling study
papers.n: Modelled patient transfers across Alberta (number of transfers not reported)
papers.finding: Ground transport more effective within 101 km; air saves 9.7 min beyond this; mixed zone to 417 km; air consistently faster beyond 417 km but 6.6 times more expensive with no modelled case where air was faster
papers.caveat: Modelling study with open/industry data; no actual patient outcomes and Canadian setting
papers.shortTitle: Modelling air vs ground EMS in Alberta

papers.title: The Role of Emergency Medical Services in Addressing Opioid Use Disorder—A Position Statement and Resource Document of NAEMSP
papers.summary: NAEMSP position statement outlining EMS roles in opioid use disorder treatment, including harm reduction, medication-assisted treatment initiation, and referral pathways.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Position statement and resource document (NAEMSP)
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Recommends scope of practice allowing prehospital buprenorphine, low-barrier MOUD protocols, naloxone distribution/harm reduction, alternate destinations, and anti-stigma education
papers.caveat: US-focused statement, not Australian policy
papers.shortTitle: NAEMSP: EMS role in opioid use disorder

papers.title: Impact of emergency medical services volume on outcomes and management in prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest: a retrospective cohort study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort examining whether higher EMS encounter volume is associated with better management and outcomes in prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective multicentre registry cohort (French RéAC)
papers.n: 6,263 traumatic OHCA cases among 151,658 OHCAs, 175 EMS bases
papers.finding: No association between EMS TCA volume and survival to hospital admission (OR 1.00; 95% CI 0.99–1.01), ROSC, 30-day survival (OR 1.01; 0.98–1.05) or favourable neurological outcome
papers.caveat: Retrospective registry data from a physician-staffed French system; limited generalisability
papers.shortTitle: EMS volume doesn't affect traumatic arrest outcomes

papers.title: Digital coordination in mass casualty incidents: a retrospective analysis of prehospital distribution times before and after IVENA-MANV implementation
papers.journal: European Journal of Trauma and Emergency Surgery
papers.summary: Retrospective evaluation of whether the IVENA-MANV digital coordination system improved prehospital distribution times during mass casualty incidents.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective observational before-after study
papers.n: 73 MCIs, 188 documented casualties (Hanover region, Germany)
papers.finding: Mean triage-to-evacuation 40.2 ± 19.3 min, total prehospital time 83.9 ± 29.5 min; no significant pre/post-IVENA-MANV differences (p > 0.05); MCI size the only significant predictor
papers.caveat: Retrospective, single region, small sample and non-randomised groups
papers.shortTitle: Digital MCI coordination didn't speed evacuation

papers.title: Field Acuity, Triage Concordance, and Clinical Outcomes in Communicative and Clinically Stable Adults Transported by 112 Ambulance Services
papers.summary: Prospective study of 393 patients transported by ambulance found urgent field classification, hypotension, critical hyperglycemia, and prehospital interventions predicted ICU admission.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Prospective single-centre observational study
papers.n: 393 communicative, clinically stable adults transported by ambulance to a tertiary ED
papers.finding: ICU admission 15.8%, 30-day mortality 5.4%. Agreement between field and ED urgency was weak (κ=0.06). Urgent field classification, critical hyperglycemia, hypotension and any prehospital intervention independently predicted ICU admission.
papers.caveat: Single Turkish centre; excluded non-communicative or unstable patients, limiting generalisability.
papers.shortTitle: Field acuity predicts ICU admission in stable adults

papers.title: Prehospital Resuscitation with Type O Whole Blood for Trauma and Hemorrhage
papers.summary: Multicenter randomized trial comparing prehospital type O whole blood resuscitation to standard care in trauma patients with hemorrhage.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Pragmatic multicentre cluster-randomised phase 3 trial with 1-month blocks
papers.n: 993 trauma patients with haemorrhagic shock transported by 44 air medical bases (695 whole blood, 298 components)
papers.finding: 30-day mortality 25.9% with whole blood vs 20.5% with blood components (adjusted OR 1.24, 95% CI 0.87–1.76; P=0.24). No difference by whole blood storage age (15–21 days vs 1–14 days: adjusted OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.74–1.32).
papers.caveat: Cluster-randomised design with unbalanced group sizes (715 vs 305 patients) may have reduced power; air medical US setting.
papers.shortTitle: Prehospital whole blood no better than components

papers.title: Alfen: a novel blind intubation device for prehospital medicine – a manikin study
papers.summary: Manikin study with 157 intubation attempts achieved >98% success rate with the novel blind intubation device across operators of varying experience.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Manikin simulation study
papers.n: 157 participants across three experience levels using three manikins
papers.finding: 155 of 157 intubation attempts succeeded (>98%); the two failures were by operators with no prior intubation experience.
papers.caveat: Manikin study only; no patient data and no comparison with standard laryngoscopy or supraglottic devices.
papers.shortTitle: Alfen blind intubation device works on manikins

papers.title: Use of double sequential external defibrillation in the United States before and after the DOSE VF randomized clinical trial
papers.summary: Nationwide observational study examined trends in DSED use for refractory VF before and after publication of the DOSE VF trial.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective interrupted time-series analysis of a national EMS data collaborative
papers.n: 16,450 adults with OHCA and VF/pVT and ≥4 defibrillation attempts from 906 agencies, 2018–2024
papers.finding: DSED use varied by identification method (1.8%–7.6%); use detected by any method increased after DOSE VF publication (7.3% vs 8.2%, p=0.048), with a rate increase of RR 1.09 (95% CI 1.04–1.14) per quarter.
papers.caveat: DSED identified by proxy measures with potential misclassification; observational design cannot link use to outcomes.
papers.shortTitle: DSED use rising but still low after DOSE VF

papers.title: Reporting of Utstein-recommended variables in prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest: a scoping review
papers.summary: Scoping review evaluated the extent to which prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest studies report Utstein-recommended variables to improve data standardization.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Scoping review (PRISMA-ScR)
papers.n: 50 prehospital TCA studies (2020–2025)
papers.finding: Core Utstein elements reported in ≥50% of studies in 72.0% vs 12.0% for supplementary; time to first shock 0%, dispatch time variables 4.0%, time to first CPR 2.0%
papers.caveat: Scoping review limited to English-language studies; descriptive only
papers.shortTitle: Poor Utstein reporting in traumatic OHCA studies

papers.title: Prehospital outcomes associated with an initial strategy of intranasal vs. intramuscular naloxone administration by EMS clinicians: a nationwide cohort study
papers.summary: Nationwide cohort study compared prehospital outcomes for initial intranasal versus intramuscular naloxone administration in suspected opioid overdose.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective nationwide EMS cohort with multilevel regression
papers.n: 16,550 adults given EMS naloxone across 1,481 agencies
papers.finding: IM vs IN: lower odds of repeat naloxone (aOR 0.39 [0.35–0.44]), lower transport odds (aOR 0.82 [0.71–0.95]), higher odds GCS >12 (aOR 1.15 [1.01–1.30]); no difference in arrest, hypoxia, agitation or nausea/vomiting treatment
papers.caveat: Retrospective database study; US setting and possible confounding by indication
papers.shortTitle: IM naloxone better than IN for overdose

papers.title: Health and Medical Preparedness and Response to the 2024 Republican National Convention
papers.summary: This case report describes comprehensive health and medical planning and multi-agency response for a large-scale national political convention, providing a template for mass gathering EMS preparedness.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Observational case report of EMS records and event planning documents
papers.n: Not reported (event attended by ~50,000 people)
papers.finding: No mass casualty incidents, mass arrests, public health emergencies or staffing crises; low patient presentation rates and on-scene prehospital care minimised impact on local health systems.
papers.caveat: Single US mass-gathering event; descriptive
papers.shortTitle: Medical planning for 2024 Republican convention

papers.title: The role of freeze-dried plasma in a world of whole blood: a Canadian prehospital and transport perspective
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: This commentary argues freeze-dried plasma complements whole blood in prehospital resuscitation, offering a scalable, shelf-stable solution for rural and remote regions with long transport times.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Narrative commentary/perspective
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Argues freeze-dried plasma is shelf-stable, pathogen-reduced and operationally feasible, complementing whole blood to extend balanced resuscitation to rural and remote Canada.
papers.caveat: Commentary without new data
papers.shortTitle: Freeze-dried plasma complements whole blood

papers.title: Duration of Emergency Medical Services-Initiated Prehospital Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Efforts and Survival for Pediatric Patients with Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
papers.summary: This nationwide cohort study examined whether longer prehospital CPR duration affects survival in paediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, finding that prolonged CPR efforts can still yield favourable neurological outcomes in selected patients.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective cohort from a US/Canada resuscitation registry
papers.n: 1,313 children with non-traumatic OHCA
papers.finding: 236 (18.0%) had prehospital ROSC; 136 (10.4%) survived to discharge. Probability of survival during ongoing EMS CPR was 7.9% at 1 min, <1% at 14.8 min, and the upper 95% CI fell below 1% at 22.0 min.
papers.caveat: Retrospective North American registry data from 2011–2015; survival probabilities are population-level, not individual predictors.
papers.shortTitle: Paediatric OHCA survival falls after ~15 min CPR

papers.title: Geographic Inequalities in Prehospital Critical Care for Cardiac Arrest: A Spatial Analysis of Deprivation and Service Configuration
papers.summary: This spatial analysis examined how deprivation levels and prehospital critical care service configuration affect cardiac arrest outcomes, revealing persistent geographic disparities in access and survival.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Spatial analysis of ambulance service data
papers.n: 57,601 OHCA patients across 9,639 English neighbourhoods
papers.finding: Median neighbourhood prehospital critical care attendance was 25.0%; attendance clustered geographically and was associated with distance to nearest critical care base. Accounting for spatial dependence removed the association with deprivation.
papers.caveat: English ambulance services only; aggregated neighbourhood-level data rather than individual patient analysis.
papers.shortTitle: Critical care attendance driven by distance, not deprivation

papers.title: Airway Management Skills and Devices on Italian Helicopter Emergency Medical Service: A National Survey
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: This national survey documented airway management skills and device availability across Italian HEMS services, showing variability in advanced airway training and device adoption.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: National cross-sectional survey of all Italian HEMS bases
papers.n: 48 of 55 active HEMS bases (87% response)
papers.finding: Videolaryngoscopes present at 81%, cricothyroidotomy kits at 94%, RSI medications universally available, but 77% provided no specific airway training, 44% required no minimum intubation number, and only 27% used prehospital airway guidelines. Mean airway preparedness index 25.7 ± 7.4 of 40.
papers.caveat: Self-reported survey data; Italian physician-staffed HEMS system not directly transferable to Australian paramedic practice.
papers.shortTitle: Italian HEMS airway equipment varies, training patchy

papers.title: Factors associated with hospital transport in emergency medical services-attended out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort of 3339 OHCA patients found 68.9% were not transported, with transport more likely in witnessed arrests, bystander CPR, hypertension, and shorter time from last known normal, and less likely with older age, malignancy, prior stroke, and arrests at home.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective population-based cohort
papers.n: 3,339 EMS-attended non-traumatic adult OHCA (Taiwan)
papers.finding: 68.9% were non-transported; transport was associated with witnessed arrest (aOR 1.754), bystander CPR (aOR 2.191), shorter/unknown last known normal (<2 h aOR 7.073), and inversely with age, malignancy, prior stroke and arrest at home; decision-maker–patient sex dyads also influenced transport odds.
papers.caveat: Single Taiwanese jurisdiction; transport decisions may not generalise to other systems
papers.shortTitle: Most EMS-attended OHCA not transported in Taiwan

papers.title: Feasibility and agreement of a self-adhesive EEG electrode set versus conventional EEG in postanoxic coma
papers.summary: Comparison of forehead EEG electrodes versus conventional EEG in 51 postanoxic coma patients found forehead recordings were interpretable in 74.1% of cases with moderate agreement, suggesting potential as a screening tool to reduce technician workload.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Prospective comparison of self-adhesive forehead EEG versus conventional EEG
papers.n: 51 postanoxic coma patients
papers.finding: Forehead recordings were of sufficient quality in 74.1% of fragments; agreement was moderate versus standard EEG (κ 0.56) and near perfect for conventional EEG visualised as forehead montage (κ 0.85); noise reduced detection of discontinuous/suppressed patterns.
papers.caveat: Moderate agreement and reduced detection of suppressed patterns due to noise; ICU setting
papers.shortTitle: Forehead EEG feasible in postanoxic coma

papers.title: Emergency Medicine Residents in the Prehospital Setting: Does This Augment Training?
papers.summary: Five-year retrospective of a physician response vehicle staffed by EM residents found residents gained valuable exposure to adult and paediatric cardiac arrests, refusals, death pronouncements, and critical trauma, with an average of 28-79 encounters per resident.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.design: Retrospective observational study of administrative records
papers.n: 90 EM residents over 5 years
papers.finding: Mean encounters per resident ranged from 28.7 (2018) to 79.2 (2022); residents managed 1,313 OHCA (34 paediatric), 1,048 refusals, 596 death pronouncements, 172 critical trauma patients and 2,053 on-line medical control consults.
papers.caveat: Single program, descriptive only; no educational outcome measures
papers.shortTitle: EM resident physician response vehicle exposure

papers.title: Utilization and Metrics Associated with Paramedic Treat and Discharge Medical Directives for Paramedic Services and Emergency Departments: A Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study analysed paramedic treat and discharge medical directives to understand utilisation patterns and key metrics for prehospital and emergency department decision-making — the findings provide valuable insights into the scope, safety, and operational impact of treat-and-refer pathways.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective cohort of paramedic records
papers.n: 1,596 patients potentially eligible for discharge directives (Ontario, Canada)
papers.finding: Of 1,596 eligible patients, 68.0% were transported, 29.7% refused transport and only 2.2% (35) were discharged by paramedics; discharged patients had half the median call duration (45 vs 87 min); among 494 linked ED patients, mean ED length of stay was 6 h 20 min and 70.2% were discharged from ED.
papers.caveat: Descriptive single-region cohort; safety and system-level impact not assessed
papers.shortTitle: Paramedic treat-and-discharge rarely used but efficient

papers.title: Can a Large Language Model Grounded in Text-Based Agency-Specific Prehospital Protocols Provide Accurate Care Recommendations?
papers.summary: This study tested whether a large language model trained on agency-specific prehospital protocol documents could generate accurate care recommendations — they found promising accuracy for protocol interpretation and clinical decision support, suggesting potential for LLMs to assist with guideline navigation at the point of care.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Non-human simulation-based experimental evaluation of a RAG-based LLM
papers.n: 6 clinical scenarios; 169 expected patient care actions
papers.finding: The LLM recommended 127 of 169 actions (75%); 5% were 'major misses' (5 of 9 in paediatric OHCA), 8% minor misses, 12% non-applicable; 12 hallucinations identified, none judged to endanger patient safety.
papers.caveat: Only six scenarios in a single EMS agency; no clinical use or patient outcomes tested
papers.shortTitle: Protocol-grounded LLM gave 75% accurate advice

papers.title: Predictive Value of Carotid Artery Doppler Ultrasound for Resuscitation Outcomes in Patients with Cardiac Arrest
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.design: Prospective observational study in one tertiary ED
papers.n: 51 adults undergoing CPR (23 ROSC, 28 non-ROSC)
papers.finding: Carotid Doppler parameters (VTI, Vmax, Vmin, TAV, MD*, RI, dv.MAX) differed significantly between ROSC and non-ROSC groups and predicted ROSC on ROC analysis.
papers.caveat: Small single-centre sample; Doppler window may have captured ROSC-transition flow; exploratory only
papers.shortTitle: Carotid Doppler parameters linked to ROSC

papers.title: Evaluation of a Situational Judgment Test for Paramedic Student Selection
papers.summary: This study validated a situational judgement test for selecting paramedic students, finding it effectively assessed non-technical skills and predicted suitability for paramedic training.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Professional position statement
papers.n: Not reported
papers.shortTitle: Professionalism as core EMS competency statement

papers.title: Eye-related emergency calls and prehospital management in region Zealand, Danmark: a register-based cohort study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Register-based cohort of 340 eye-related emergency calls found chemical exposures (31.5%), vision loss (25.9%), and trauma (18.2%) as leading causes, with 11.5% of patients initially coded for eye problems later diagnosed with stroke.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective register-based cohort study linking dispatch, prehospital and national patient registries
papers.n: 340 eye-related emergency calls, Region Zealand, Denmark
papers.finding: Leading causes: chemical exposure 31.5%, vision loss 25.9%, ocular trauma 18.2%. 11.5% suspected stroke prehospitally; 7.4% of admitted patients had confirmed TIA/stroke. Irrigation documented in 27.1%.
papers.caveat: Single Danish region, descriptive registry design with reliance on documentation
papers.shortTitle: Eye emergency calls often chemical or stroke

papers.title: Prophylaxis of opioid-induced nausea in helicopter emergency medical service: a prospective quasi-experimental study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Prospective study of 205 HEMS patients comparing ondansetron prophylaxis, aromatherapy, and no prophylaxis for opioid-induced nausea — neither intervention showed benefit compared to no prophylaxis in unselected patients.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Prospective quasi-experimental rotating-schedule study across six HEMS bases
papers.n: 205 patients >16 given opioids for traumatic pain (86 no prophylaxis, 64 ondansetron, 55 aromatherapy)
papers.finding: Median NRS change 0 in all groups; NRS increase in 15%, 14%, 15%; NRS>3 in 14% vs 11% vs 11%; vomiting 4%, 2%, 0%. Neither ondansetron nor aromatherapy showed benefit over no prophylaxis.
papers.caveat: Quasi-experimental rotating allocation, single HEMS system, modest sample size
papers.shortTitle: No benefit from prophylaxis for opioid nausea

papers.title: Intranasal Versus Intramuscular Midazolam in Pediatric Seizure Control: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.summary: Meta-analysis testing whether intranasal or intramuscular midazolam works better for paediatric seizures without cannula access — intramuscular midazolam was associated with faster seizure termination and less need for rescue therapy, especially in the prehospital setting.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis (random-effects)
papers.n: 5 studies, 3,933 paediatric seizure patients (97.9% prehospital)
papers.finding: IM midazolam associated with less rescue therapy (RR 1.29; 95% CI 1.15–1.45), shorter time to seizure termination (MD 23.60 s; 95% CI 2.31–44.89), persisting at 0.2 mg/kg dose.
papers.caveat: Only five studies, observational comparison of routes with possible confounding
papers.shortTitle: IM beats intranasal midazolam in paediatric seizures

papers.title: Manual versus Automated Ventilation with an i-gel® Airway During Short-Haul Helicopter Operations
papers.summary: Simulation study comparing bag-valve ventilation with automated ventilation during short-haul helicopter rescue using an i-gel — automated ventilation achieved target minute ventilation more consistently, caused less airway movement, and avoided disconnects.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Prospective simulation crossover study with manikin and i-gel
papers.n: 9 stretcher attendants (static), 6 (live) short-haul tests
papers.finding: Automated ventilation achieved target minute ventilation in 100% of tests vs 67% (static) and 33% (live) manual; manual caused greater i-gel movement and four disconnects vs none (differences not statistically significant, p=0.25 and 0.12).
papers.caveat: Very small simulation study, manikin only, not statistically powered
papers.shortTitle: Automated ventilation wins in helicopter short-haul

papers.title: The role of tactical police medics in the prehospital environment: results from an interview study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Interview study exploring how Swedish tactical police medics view their training, role, and real-world practice — they reported being well trained but underused, with scope restrictions and inconsistent collaboration limiting what they can actually do.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Low
papers.design: Qualitative semi-structured interview study
papers.n: 13 Swedish tactical police medics
papers.finding: Medics were satisfied with training but reported a mismatch between training and actual tasks, restrictions preventing care for third parties, and inconsistent collaboration with ambulance services.
papers.caveat: Small single-country qualitative sample, not generalisable
papers.shortTitle: Tactical police medics trained but underused

papers.title: Paramedics' decisions to withhold resuscitation in traumatic cardiac arrest: accuracy of paramedic assessments compared with autopsy findings
papers.summary: Retrospective Ontario review testing how paramedics decide to withhold CPR in traumatic cardiac arrest — most no-CPR decisions were based on signs clearly incompatible with life, and post-mortem findings supported paramedic assessment in the large majority of cases.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective coroner case file review
papers.n: 90 prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest cases without CPR
papers.finding: 61% had documented injuries incompatible with life or signs of irreversible death; postmortem confirmed incompatible injuries in 89% of these. Of 35 cases withholding CPR on other grounds, 83% had postmortem injuries making arrest irreversible.
papers.caveat: Retrospective, single region (Ontario, Canada) with only cases where CPR was withheld and EMS records available
papers.shortTitle: Paramedics accurate withholding CPR in traumatic arrest

papers.title: The impact of advanced pre-hospital interventions on scene time
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Retrospective physician-led HEMS trauma study examining whether more advanced interventions are stretching scene times — each additional intervention increased scene time by 41%, although overall scene times stayed similar over two decades because of changing case mix.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective observational study of physician-led air ambulance
papers.n: 1,357 injured patients
papers.finding: 26% received an advanced intervention; each additional intervention increased scene time by 41% (p<0.001). Median scene times stayed similar between 2005–2010 and 2017–2021 (10 vs 25 min penetrating vs blunt, p<0.001).
papers.caveat: Retrospective, single physician-led HEMS service; July-only sampling of each year
papers.shortTitle: Each advanced prehospital intervention adds scene time

papers.title: Out-of-Hospital Management of Suspected Spinal Cord Injuries: How Much Evidence Does it Take to Change Practice?
papers.summary: Commentary challenging continued routine spinal immobilisation in suspected spinal injury — the authors argue decades of evidence now consistently show harm without benefit, and that paramedic scope should evolve to reflect current evidence.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Letter to the editor / commentary
papers.shortTitle: Call to abandon routine spinal immobilisation

papers.title: Early Intensive Blood Pressure Reduction After Intracerebral Hemorrhage Is Associated With Worse Functional Outcome: The Risk of Overshooting Blood Pressure Goals
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort testing whether rapid systolic BP reduction ≤150 mm Hg after spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage improved outcomes — early target achievement and overshooting <120 mm Hg were associated with worse functional outcome.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective cohort at two academic EDs
papers.n: 420 adults with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage
papers.finding: Achieving systolic BP ≤150 mmHg within 2 hours was associated with worse functional outcome (OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.17–4.57), as was overshooting below 120 mmHg within 6 hours (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.27–5.13)
papers.caveat: Retrospective design with possible confounding by haemorrhage severity; in-hospital ED population
papers.shortTitle: Overshooting BP targets worsens ICH outcomes

papers.title: No delayed intracranial hemorrhage in head injury patients on oral anticoagulants and with normal CT: a retrospective study of 215 patients
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Retrospective review tested whether immediate discharge after normal CT was safe for anticoagulated head-injury patients with GCS 14-15 — no delayed intracranial haemorrhage, neurosurgical intervention, or clinically significant deterioration occurred.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective single-centre review
papers.n: 215 anticoagulated head injury patients with normal head CT (median age 83)
papers.finding: Zero delayed intracranial haemorrhages; no neurosurgical interventions or clinically significant deterioration due to delayed haemorrhage during observation or follow-up
papers.caveat: Retrospective single-centre study with limited follow-up; small sample cannot exclude rare events
papers.shortTitle: Normal CT safely rules out delayed bleed on anticoagulants

papers.title: Comparison of needle decompression to simple (finger) thoracostomy in non-perfused cadaveric models with theoretical tension pneumothorax
papers.summary: Cadaveric crossover study testing needle decompression versus simple thoracostomy for theoretical tension pneumothorax — simple thoracostomy was more successful and faster, but the model limits clinical certainty.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Prospective simulation-based experimental crossover study in fresh cadavers
papers.n: 38 paired attempts in cadaveric models
papers.finding: Simple thoracostomy relieved theoretical tension pneumothorax in 92.1% vs 76.3% for needle decompression; full relief to 0 mmHg in 60.5% vs 28.9% (p = 0.004); thoracostomy was faster (11.9 vs 34.1 s)
papers.caveat: Cadaveric model with artificially created tension pneumothorax; may not reflect clinical performance
papers.shortTitle: Finger thoracostomy beats needle decompression in cadavers

papers.title: Healthcare costs of expedited transport compared with standard care following out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: results from the EVIDENCE randomised controlled trial
papers.summary: Greater Sydney costing analysis of expedited OHCA transport for possible ECPR versus standard care — overall health system costs were comparable, with higher costs when patients arrived during ECPR business hours.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Prospective health system costing analysis alongside the EVIDENCE randomised trial in Greater Sydney
papers.n: 197 OHCA patients (102 expedited, 95 standard care)
papers.finding: Mean costs per patient AUD$60,780 (expedited) vs $67,579 (standard care); difference -$6,799 (95% CI -$44,014 to $30,416), not significant; costs were $36,182 higher within ECPR hours (95% CI $1,554–72,918)
papers.caveat: Costing from a single trial in one system; costs estimated without formal economic evaluation of outcomes
papers.shortTitle: Expedited OHCA transport costs similar to standard

papers.title: Effect of vascular access strategy on long-term outcomes in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a randomised clinical trial
papers.summary: IVIO follow-up comparing initial intraosseous versus intravenous access in adult non-traumatic OHCA — 6-month and 1-year outcomes were similar, with no evidence that either access strategy improves long-term survival or neurological outcome.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Follow-up of the IVIO randomised clinical trial
papers.n: 1,479 adults with non-traumatic OHCA
papers.finding: At 1 year, survival 11% (IO) vs 9% (IV), RR 1.24 (95% CI 0.91–1.67); favourable neurological outcome 10% vs 8%, RR 1.28 (95% CI 0.93–1.77); mean EQ-5D-5L score 83 vs 76 (difference 7, 95% CI 1–13)
papers.caveat: Non-significant point estimates favouring IO; survivors-only quality-of-life comparison may be underpowered
papers.shortTitle: IV vs IO in OHCA: long-term outcomes similar

papers.title: The Estimated Benefit of Lights and Sirens During Ambulance Transport
papers.summary: This study used a modern transport model to estimate whether lights and sirens save time, and it found a median gain of only 3.0 to 3.3 minutes per trip, which likely does not justify the known driving risks except in selected cases.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Observational study comparing actual emergent trips with modelled non-emergent trip durations
papers.n: 25,902 incidents, 21.0% transported with lights and sirens
papers.finding: Lights and sirens were associated with a median trip duration saving of 3.0 min (95% CI 2.9–3.1), or 3.3 min in spatially aggregated analysis, and 0.3 min/km faster pace
papers.caveat: Modelled non-emergent comparisons in a single US EMS system; median benefit may hide variation by case type
papers.shortTitle: Lights and sirens save only ~3 minutes

papers.title: Statewide Emergency Medical Services Protocols for Field-Initiated Blood Resuscitation
papers.design: Cross-sectional review of publicly available statewide EMS protocols
papers.n: 32 statewide protocols (31 states plus DC)
papers.finding: 13 of 32 (42%) protocols allowed field-initiated blood transfusion; all allowed trauma use, 69% allowed medical use, 69% allowed paediatric transfusion, 23% specified low titer O whole blood, and only 31% addressed biologically female patients
papers.caveat: US protocols only; descriptive, not linked to patient outcomes, and excludes critical care/interfacility protocols
papers.shortTitle: US statewide protocols for prehospital blood vary

papers.title: The impact of defibrillation current and pad position on return of spontaneous circulation during refractory ventricular fibrillation
papers.summary: Secondary analysis of DOSE VF examined whether transthoracic current, pad position, and ROSC were linked, and found AP pad placement delivered higher current and was independently associated with ROSC, while delivered current itself was not.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Secondary per-protocol analysis of the DOSE VF randomised trial
papers.n: 342 patients with refractory VF (849 shocks)
papers.finding: AP shocks delivered higher current (VC 19.6 A, DSED 19.2 A) than AL shocks (16.6 A) and DSED AL (17.3 A); AP pad position, but not delivered current, was independently associated with ROSC
papers.caveat: Secondary analysis of a trial population; observational within-trial associations, not a randomised comparison of pad position itself
papers.shortTitle: AP pad position, not current, predicts ROSC

papers.title: Feasibility of portable telemedicine devices for ambulance-based prehospital triage: a comparative simulation study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Simulation study comparing portable telemedicine devices for ambulance triage, and found the Vuzix headset ranked highest overall, but the smartphone app was the most practical early implementation option.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Comparative simulation study with multi-criteria decision analysis
papers.n: 47 surveys from ambulance professionals, remote neurologists and a patient actor across four simulated stroke-like scenarios
papers.finding: Vuzix head-mounted device ranked highest (value score 0.80), ahead of Siilo smartphone app (0.77) and RealWear (0.73); ambulance crews favoured smartphone usability, neurologists favoured Vuzix video quality
papers.caveat: Simulation setting only; no clinical or operational impact assessed
papers.shortTitle: Portable telemedicine devices compared for triage

papers.title: The Effect of Lights and Sirens on Critical Care Transport Time
papers.summary: They measured whether lights and sirens meaningfully shorten critical care transport, and found a statistically significant but modest time saving of about 8 minutes.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Retrospective cohort of ED CPR following prehospital-initiated resuscitation
papers.n: 818 non-traumatic OHCA patients (345 manual, 473 mechanical CPR)
papers.finding: No significant difference in 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month mortality (12-month p=0.034); favourable neurological outcome (mRS ≤3 at 1 year) 3.5% vs 4.0% (p=0.501)
papers.caveat: Retrospective design in the ED setting; findings may not apply to prehospital compression choice
papers.shortTitle: Mechanical vs manual CPR shows no survival difference

papers.title: Feasibility of a Pre-Hospital Virtual Triage and Care Model: A Mixed-Methods Pilot in Emergency Care
papers.summary: They tested a pre-hospital telehealth model for ambulance-retrieved patients, and found it was feasible, advanced senior review, and reduced ED length of stay without improving crew cycle times.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Mixed-methods pilot with matched cohort analysis
papers.n: 26 eligible patients; piloted in 10 cases over 3 days
papers.finding: Senior medical assessment 81 minutes earlier, ED length of stay reduced 14% (50 minutes); no improvement in crew cycle times; high patient satisfaction
papers.caveat: Very small pilot sample (10 cases) over 3 days
papers.shortTitle: Virtual triage model feasible for ambulance patients

papers.title: Sonorheometry to detect traumatic induced coagulopathy during initial management of trauma patients: an observational, multi-center study
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Tested whether Quantra can rapidly detect trauma-induced coagulopathy against standard lab tests, and found early Quantra analysis may reliably exclude TIC, but prospective validation is still needed.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Multicentre observational diagnostic accuracy study at four level-1 trauma centres
papers.n: 504 severe trauma patients >16 years (285 derivation, 219 validation)
papers.finding: AUCs 0.82–0.91 for detecting TIC thresholds; in validation, negative predictive values 0.88–1.00 but positive predictive values only 0.13–0.67
papers.caveat: In-hospital testing at level-1 trauma centres, not prehospital; low PPV and prospective validation still required
papers.shortTitle: Quantra sonorheometry rules out trauma coagulopathy

papers.title: Chest X-Ray evaluation using GPT for tube thoracostomy or conservative care in non-tension spontaneous pneumothorax
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Tested whether a vision-enabled GPT model could estimate pneumothorax size and guide tube thoracostomy vs conservative care, and it matched radiologist measurements closely with good agreement to real-world ED decisions.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.design: Single-centre retrospective observational study of vision-enabled GPT on chest radiographs
papers.n: 101 adults with confirmed spontaneous pneumothorax
papers.finding: Sensitivity 86.8%, specificity 93.8%, accuracy 90.1%, AUC 0.90 for tube thoracostomy within 24h; depth agreement ICC 0.893, MAE 0.69 cm
papers.caveat: Single-centre retrospective design with confirmed pneumothorax only; no prehospital or prospective testing
papers.shortTitle: GPT estimates pneumothorax size to guide care

papers.title: Paramedic Patella Reduction — Ambulance Victoria CPG Evaluation
papers.summary: Retrospective study (n=1,210) evaluating whether Ambulance Victoria's Nov 2022 CPG for paramedic patella reduction changed practice — 91.8% reduction success rate, transport rate dropped 38.4%, case duration cut by ~33 minutes, and IV cannula use down 17.3%, with no change in effective analgesia rates.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High
papers.design: Retrospective interrupted time series using Ambulance Victoria electronic patient care data
papers.n: 1,210 patients with acute patella dislocation (622 pre-, 588 post-guideline)
papers.finding: No significant step change in effective analgesia (0.8%, 95%CI -6.6% to 8.1%; p=0.832); significant reductions in IV access (-17.3%), transport rate (-38.4%) and case duration (~33 minutes shorter)
papers.caveat: Retrospective design; analgesia unchanged, and longer-term functional outcomes and safety not assessed
papers.shortTitle: Paramedic patella reduction guideline works in Victoria

papers.title: Delayed Defibrillation of Ventricular Arrhythmias During Transcutaneous Pacing
papers.summary: Case series examining the problem of ventricular arrhythmias occurring during TCP and delays to defibrillation — highlights the clinical trap of pacing artefact masking VF and the need to pause pacing to identify shockable rhythms.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.shortTitle: Pacing artefact can mask VF during TCP

papers.title: The Diamond Minutes: Rethinking the Earliest Link of the Trauma Chain of Survival
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.summary: Concept editorial arguing that the first minutes after injury, before EMS arrival, are a distinct high-risk window where bystander action and dispatcher guidance can prevent deaths, especially through haemorrhage control and airway management.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium
papers.shortTitle: Bystander care in first minutes of trauma

weeklyTldr.summary:
Minithoracostomy matched chest drainage on scene time and had fewer recorded complications in a physician-led HEMS cohort — hypothesis-generating, not practice-changing.
Flush-rate NRB remains the preoxygenation standard — adding a nasal cannula at 15–25 L/min was clearly inferior in healthy volunteers.
Australian audit of the Victorian Heart Hospital cardiac ED: 50.4% survival to discharge in a selected post-ROSC cohort, with a 24% interhospital transfer rate.
Only 1% of non-transported children re-called within 72 hours across 1.85 million US paediatric ambulance calls — deaths after non-transport were rare.

topPicks.title: Prehospital Minithoracostomy versus Chest Drainage for Emergency Pleural Decompression in Major Trauma
topPicks.authors: Serena Tomasino, Daniele Orso, Maria Grandesso, et al.
topPicks.summary: Retrospective physician-led HEMS cohort (94 trauma patients) comparing prehospital minithoracostomy with chest drainage — minithoracostomy carried no meaningful scene-time penalty and fewer recorded complications, but non-random allocation and few events make it hypothesis-generating only.
topPicks.relevance: 🟡 Medium transferability — surgical pleural decompression isn't in the extracted ACTAS guidelines (CMG 17 covers needle decompression, ICP-flagged); would need a guideline change to adopt
topPicks.featuredReason: Tension pneumothorax decompression is a problem crews face with far fewer tools than physician-led HEMS — this is the first direct head-to-head of the two techniques and it's honest about its limits.
topPicks.design: Retrospective physician-led HEMS cohort with Bayesian analysis
topPicks.n: 94 major trauma adults (66 minithoracostomy, 28 chest drainage)
topPicks.finding: Posterior median scene-time difference −5.9 minutes (95% CrI −13.8 to 1.7); recorded complications 0/50 evaluable minithoracostomy vs 6/10 evaluable chest drainage (risk difference −58.7 percentage points, 95% CrI −83.9 to −29.3); no clear survival differences at 1, 30 or 90 days.
topPicks.caveat: Non-randomised allocation by clinical judgment, complication ascertainment differed between groups, and very few events.

topPicks.title: Combined NRB and Nasal Cannula Oxygen Delivery Is Inferior to Flush Rate NRB for Emergency Preoxygenation
topPicks.authors: Andrew M. Pearson, Eli R. Haddorff, Alec J. Bunting, et al.
topPicks.summary: Healthy-volunteer crossover study — NRB plus nasal cannula at 15–25 L/min each produced expired oxygen of 68–75% versus 85% for flush-rate NRB, so the portable-cylinder workaround is inferior when supply allows flush rate.
topPicks.relevance: 🟢 High transferability — uses only kit in ACTAS scope (NRB, nasal cannula, oxygen) and applies from AP airway care through ICP pre-RSI
topPicks.featuredReason: Directly informs how you manage limited oxygen supply away from the vehicle: the popular NRB-plus-nasal-cannula combo costs 10–16 points of expired oxygen versus flush rate.
topPicks.design: Experimental crossover study in healthy volunteers
topPicks.finding: Mean FeO2: flush-rate NRB 85% vs 68% (NRB + nasal cannula at 15 L/min each) and 75% (at 25 L/min each); differences of 16% (95% CI 13–20%) and 10% (95% CI 6–14%), both failing non-inferiority.
topPicks.caveat: Healthy volunteers in a controlled setting, not patients requiring emergency airway management.
topPicks.shortTitle: NRB + nasal cannula inferior to flush-rate preoxygenation

topPicks.title: Postresuscitation Out‐of‐Hospital Cardiac Arrest Presentations to Australia's First Dedicated Cardiac Hospital: A Retrospective Audit of Outcomes and Emergency Department Access Factors
topPicks.authors: Thenul Munasinghe, Kaylie Shaw, Claire Charteris, et al.
topPicks.summary: Audit of 121 post-arrest patients at the Victorian Heart Hospital — 50.4% survived to discharge with 92.6% prehospital ROSC and 61.2% shockable rhythms, and 24% needed interhospital transfer, mostly for non-cardiac causes.
topPicks.relevance: 🟢 High transferability — Australian post-ROSC outcomes data relevant to CMG 4A transport and destination decisions, though ACT has no dedicated cardiac hospital equivalent
topPicks.featuredReason: Fifty per cent survival in a selected cohort plus a 24% interhospital transfer rate keeps the destination-after-ROSC question alive — a system issue paramedic routing decisions feed directly.
topPicks.design: Retrospective audit of a dedicated cardiac hospital ED
topPicks.finding: Survival to discharge 50.4%; 30-day survival 40.0%; shockable rhythms 61.2%, prehospital ROSC 92.6%; shockable rhythm (OR 3.46), cardiac aetiology (OR 3.40) and prehospital ROSC (OR 9.23) associated with survival; 24.0% needed interhospital transfer.
topPicks.caveat: Small, single highly selected tertiary cohort not comparable to population-based OHCA outcomes.
topPicks.shortTitle: Post-OHCA outcomes at Victorian Heart Hospital
